en: For you, O Agni, were the first inventor of this prayer, the wondrous invoker.
O bull, you have made that strength unassailable, a power to overcome every power.
Then you sat down as the most excellent sacrificer in the place of worship, the one worthy of praise, seeking to provide nourishment.
To you, the first, the men seeking the gods have gone, perceiving you for the sake of great wealth.
Following you as you go with many riches like a chosen host, they who are watchful have followed after your wealth—
the radiant Agni, beautiful to behold, vast, rich in fatness, shining forevermore.
Seeking glory, they have attained imperishable glory by approaching with reverence the station of the god;
they have even assumed names worthy of sacrifice, delighting in your auspicious appearance. The peoples on earth increase you; both kinds of people seek wealth from you.
You are the protector, worthy of being known in our crossing over; you have truly become father and mother to human beings.
Worthy of worship, beloved among the people, Agni—the joyous invoker—has sat down as the most skilled sacrificer.
To you, shining brightly within our home, we shall sit with reverence, bowing down in homage.
We, seeking your favor and desiring the gods, approach you, O Agni—the wise one, the new—with pure thoughts.
You, O Agni, have led the people, shining with the great light of heaven.
The sage of the people, the lord of eternal tribes, the subduer, the bull among men.
RV 6.1.8: [We praise] Agni, the purifier, who shines forth, looking with both the open and the blinking eye, the radiant one, the worshipful lord of riches.
RV 6.1.9: That mortal, O Agni, has sacrificed and performed his labor who has attained your gift of oblation with fuel;
he who knows the offering thoroughly with prostrations—he, being protected by you, shall possess all desirable things.
To you, the great one, we shall pay worship with great homage, O Agni, with fuel and with oblations. On the altar, O Son of Strength, with songs and hymns, may we strive for your auspicious favor.
He who has overspread the two worlds with light and with glories, he who is glorious and a conqueror.
O Agni, shine forth far and wide for us with great, enduring, and wealthy spoils.
O Vasu, grant us evermore the wealth of men; bestow upon our children and descendants abundant cattle and many great refreshments.
May misfortunes remain far away, and may auspicious glories of renown attend us.

O King Agni, through my devotion to you, may I obtain many riches in manifold ways from your wealth. For in you, O Agni, who possess many boons, there are many treasures for the one who serves you, the king.
For you, O Agni, like Mitra, possess lordly glory that shines over the settlements.
O all-beholding Vasu, you nourish renown and prosperity as if it were your own growth.
For indeed, the people honor you with sacrifices and songs;
to you the prize-winning steed, free from malice, speeds across the mid-air, beholding all people.
In unison, the men of heaven kindle you, the banner of the sacrifice,
when this human folk, seeking favor, invokes you at the ritual. May the mortal who exerts himself with prayer for you, the bounteous giver, be successful.
Through his aid, he crosses over enmity and distress from the vast heaven.
The mortal who, with fuel, attains your oblation and your sharpening power,
O Agni— he nourishes a household rich in offspring and lasting a hundred years.
Your brilliant smoke rises up, bright and extended across the sky;
for like the sun in its splendor, O Purifier, you shine with your radiant form.
For thus you are to be honored among the people, our beloved guest.
Delightful like an ancient stronghold, worthy of trust like a son;
for by your wisdom, O Agni, you are anointed in the wooden vat like a prize-winning steed.
Like a self-sustaining wanderer, like a home, like a swift horse that does not stray—you are a youngling.
O Agni, you consume even those things that are immovable, like cattle in a pasture; for when your skillful [priests] cut down the forests, O ageless one, they strike at your very foundations.
For you, O Agni, enter as the Hotṛ-priest into the house of the people who perform the sacrifice.
O Lord of the People, bring us prosperity; O Aṅgiras, enjoy our oblation.
O Agni, god of Mitra-like majesty, speak for us to the gods and to the favor of Heaven and Earth.
Attain well-being and a secure dwelling from the men of heaven; may we cross over our enemies, distresses, and misfortunes—may we cross them, may we cross them through your protection.

O Agni, he shall dwell in peace, a guardian of Truth born of Truth; seeking the gods, he attains your wide light— that mortal whom you, O God, together with Mitra and Varuṇa, protect with your power from distress.
He has sacrificed with sacrifices, he has labored with holy rites; he has given gifts to Agni, whose doors are prosperous.
Even so, no lack of glory, no distress, and no arrogance reaches that mortal who is favored by you.
Like the sun, his appearance is stainless; when he goes forth in his brilliance, his thought is formidable.
Like a neighing steed, he is not to be held back at night; wherever he dwells, the forest-born one is delightful.
His form is sharp and great; like a horse controlled by the reins, he moves with his mouth. Licking [the wood], like an axe, his tongue—like a smelter, he melts the wood while burning it.
Like an archer aiming at a target, he hurls [his flame]; he sharpens his brilliance like the edge of iron.
He whose course is variegated, the unassailable one, who like the dawn from darkness speeds along with rapid flight, resting upon the wood.
Like a singer, he clothes himself in the rays of light; with his flame, he of Mitra-like greatness, cries out aloud.
He who is ruddy by night and by day for men, the immortal one, ruddy by day for men.
Like the roar of heaven when it bestows gifts, the bull has bellowed; he has roared among the plants.
Like one driven by heat, moving with a swift flight, he has filled the two worlds, the well-wedded pair, with wealth.
He who, like lightning, has flashed forth with his own powers, with nourishing and fitting hymns of praise.

Or he who has fashioned the host of the Maruts, like R̥bhu— he has shone forth, impetuous and fierce. Just as you, O Son of Strength, perform the sacrifice for the gods at the divine assembly of man with offerings,
so today, O Agni, desiring them, worship the yearning gods equally for us all in this common rite.
May he, the radiant Agni, who is like the eye that beholds at dawn, grant us wealth—he who is worthy of praise and to be known.
He who is immortal among mortals, the all-enlivening one, has become the guest who awakens at daybreak, Jātavedas.
Like the heavens, they marvel at his vast power; bright as the sun, he clothes himself in splendors.
He who, ageless and purifying, impels [the world], has shattered even the ancient works of Aśna. For you, O Son, are a speaker; Agni, by his very birth, has established food as his path.
As such, O bestower of strength, bestow strength upon us; like a king, may we dwell in a place free from wolves.
He who sharpens his weapons and devours the resisting food passes through the nights like Vāyu, the sovereign lord.
May we overcome those who oppose your commands, as a swift horse avoids falling pitfalls. Like the sun with its radiant beams, O Agni, you have overspread both heaven and earth with your light.
Variegated and anointed with brilliance, he leads us beyond the darkness; like Auśija flying in his flight, he hastens with his flame.
For we have chosen you, the most delightful one, with the flames of our hymns; hear our great cry, O Agni!
Like Indra, no other deity fills you with power; the most truthful ones satisfy you with their bounty.
Now, O Agni, lead us safely by paths free from enemies toward wealth; carry us across distress.
Grant those blessings to our patrons and to the singer; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
I invoke for you the Son of Strength, the youthful one, whose speech is guileless, the youngest, with my prayers.
The wise one, who bestows all desirable treasures and many gifts, is free from malice.
O Hotṛ of many aspects, the worshipful ones have placed their treasures in you at evening and at dawn.
In him, the radiant one, all beings and all blessings have been gathered together, as if upon the earth.
From of old you have sat among these people; by your wisdom, you became the charioteer of desirable things.
Therefore, O wise Jātavedas, you bestow riches in succession upon the one who serves you.
O Agni, he who from afar seeks to harm us, or he who, though great as Mitra, would attack us from within—[drive him away].

O most burning burner, you who are rich in heat through your own unaging, bull-like flames— O Son of Strength, he who serves you with sacrifice, with fuel, with hymns, and with songs of praise— he, O Immortal One, being wise among mortals, shines forth with wealth, splendor, and renown.
O Agni, do that which is desired and praised; O powerful one, overcome our rivals with your might.
Since you are celebrated with words throughout the days, take pleasure in this; hear the prayer of the singer.
May we attain that desire through your protection, O Agni; may we attain wealth, O Lord of riches, together with heroic sons.
May we, seeking booty, obtain booty; may we obtain from you, O ageless one, undecaying splendor.
Seeking a path by means of sacrifice with a new [hymn], he approaches the Son of Strength.
Cutting down the forest, the divine Hotṛ goes toward the bright one whose path is black, for the sake of the feast.
He, the whitening one, thundering, dwelling in the luminous realm, most youthful with his ageless,
roaring flames— he who is the purifier, most frequent, Agni, who goes along devouring many broad things.
O pure Agni, thy pure, wind-driven beams spread forth in every direction.
The divine Navagvas, exceedingly destructive, boldly strike down the forests as they break them apart.
O Radiant One, those bright and pure steeds of yours, when let loose, shear the earth bare.
Then your whirling flame shines far and wide, sweeping across the ridges of the dappled earth.
Then the tongue of the Bull, who fights for cattle, darts forth like a released thunderbolt;
like the snare of a hero, the consuming power of Agni, difficult to restrain and terrible, devours the forests.
With the radiance of that great impeller, you have boldly overspread the earthly expanses.
Drive away those fears with your powers; as you strive, burn down the rivals and the seekers of wealth.
O Wondrous One, bestow upon us wondrous, wondrously perceiving, most wondrous power over dominion, and a source of vitality.
O Radiant One, grant to the singer radiant, vast wealth consisting of many heroes, through your radiant rays.
The gods have generated Agni Vaiśvānara— the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, born in the cosmic order (ṛta)—
the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men, as a vessel for their mouths. Him, the navel of sacrifices, the seat of riches, the great reservoir, they have celebrated with songs.
The gods have generated Vaiśvānara, the charioteer of sacrifices, the banner of the ritual.
From you, O Agni, is born the inspired singer; from you come the heroes who overcome the enemy.
O King Vaiśvānara, bestow upon us desirable riches.
O Immortal One, all the gods sing out to you in unison as you are born, like unto a newborn infant.
Through your mental powers (*kratubhiḥ*), O Vaiśvānara, they attained immortality when you shone forth from your two parents.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, no one has ever dared to violate those great ordinances (*vratāni*) of yours.
When you were being born in the lap of your parents, you found the banner in the appointed places of the days.
By the eye of Vaiśvānara and by the banner of immortality, the ridges of heaven were measured out.
Upon his head indeed all beings have grown, like branches, the seven spreading streams.
He of skillful wisdom who measured out the realms, Vaiśvānara, the seer who spanned the luminous spheres of heaven;
he who has spread himself around all living beings, the undeceived guardian and protector of immortality—
now I shall proclaim the conquering power of the ruddy bull, of Jātavedas, from the assembly of knowledge.

For Vaiśvānara, a newer, pure thought flows forth like the beautiful Soma; it purifies itself for Agni. Being born in the highest heaven, Agni, the guardian of vows, protected the sacred laws. With his skillful wisdom, Vaiśvānara measured out the mid-air and touched the firmament with his greatness.
The wondrous Mitra propped apart heaven and earth; he drove away the darkness with light within the two worlds.
Vaiśvānara rolled out the two bowls like skins and assumed all manly vigor.
In the lap of the waters, the mighty ones seized him; the clans waited upon the King, the one worthy of praise.
Mātariśvan brought Agni Vaiśvānara hither from afar as a messenger from Vivasvat.
O Agni, age after age, bestow upon those who praise you a wealth that is worthy of the assembly, glorious, and ever new.
O King, O ageless one, like a sharp blade, strike down the evildoer with your splendor, as one fells a tree.
O Agni, maintain for us among our patrons an unaging sovereignty and great heroic power.

O Vaiśvānara, may we win through your protections a hundredfold and thousandfold prize, O Agni. With your unfailing guardians, O Desired One, protect our wise patrons, O you who abide in the three places.
And grant us protection, O Agni Vaiśvānara; may the host of those who give be praised as they advance.
The dark day and the bright day revolve by means of their distinct knowledges;
as he is born, Agni Vaiśvānara, like a king, has driven away the darkness with his light.
I do not know the warp, nor do I know the woof, nor that which they weave as they strive together in the contest.
Who indeed, being a son here, can speak of things beyond his father who is below him?
He alone knows the warp, he knows the woof; he shall speak the words of wisdom in their proper season.
He who has perceived him as the guardian of immortality, moving below while looking beyond through another;
this is the first Hotṛ—behold him! This is the immortal light among mortals. He was born, firmly established and seated, the immortal one increasing in his body.
A firm light has been established for sight; the mind, the swiftest among those that fly, is within. All the gods, of one mind and one intention, move successfully toward a single purpose.
My two ears fly apart, my vision spreads wide—this light which is placed within my heart.
My mind wanders, its thoughts reaching far; what indeed shall I say, and what now shall I imagine?
All the gods, struck with fear, paid homage to you, O Agni, as you stood in the darkness. May Vaiśvānara protect us for our aid; may the Immortal protect us for our aid.
Place before you at the commencement of the sacrifice the delightful, celestial Agni, worthy of fair praise, as you perform the rite.
Place him before you with hymns, for he, our radiant Jātavedas, shall make our sacrifices successful.
O brilliant Hotṛ Agni, kindled by the fires of Manu, you who possess many faces—
The hymn which they purify for him like strength, like bright ghee, with their thoughts— He,
the inspired singer who has given to Agni with hymns, thrives with glory among mortals. To him, the one of wondrous luster, he grants various aids at the winning of the cow-stall.

He who, at his birth, filled the two wide worlds, he whose path is black, who is visible from afar with his light; even through the thickest darkness of the night, that Purifier has become manifest with his flame.
Now, O Agni, bestow upon us and upon our patrons wonderful wealth, accompanied by many strengths and aids!

RV 6.10.5: Those who, by their bounty and their fame, surpass others, and by their heroic deeds excel over men— RV 6.10.6: O Agni, desiring it, accept this sacrifice which the offerer of oblations, sitting here, presents to you with his mouth. Among the Bharadvājas, you have accepted the well-fashioned hymn for the winning of booty that is to be seized.
Drive away hostilities; increase our nourishment. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.

O Agni, being impelled, sacrifice as the most skilled sacrificer at the *hotṛ*-priest’s office, like the irresistible urging of the Maruts. May Mitra and Varuṇa, the Nāsatyas, Heaven and Earth, turn hither to our sacrificial offering.
You are our most delightful invoker, O guileless god, among mortals at the assemblies.
As the bearer [of the sacrifice], O Agni, with your purifying tongue and mouth, worship your own self.
For even the bountiful prayer desires you; let it bring the gods to the one who sings their praise, so that he may sacrifice.
When the inspired sage, the most trembling among the Aṅgirases, the seer Rebha, utters the sweet song at the sacrifice;
then, O Agni of brilliant skill, you have shone forth with radiant light—sacrifice to the two wide-reaching worlds, Heaven and Earth.
Him whom the five peoples, offering oblations with reverence, anoint like a long-lived man, he who is rich in nourishment.

I spread the sacred grass with reverence before Agni; the ladle, filled with clarified butter, is offered with a well-fashioned hymn. The seat has been established upon the dwelling-place of the earth; the sacrifice has been set forth like the eye of the sun.
O Agni, you of many aspects, being kindled with the fires by the gods, grant us your favor, O Hotṛ-priest.
O Son of Strength, clothed in riches, may we pass beyond distress as if across a narrow pass.
The Hotṛ-priest, the sovereign upon the sacred grass within the dwelling, Agni, shall worship both Heaven and Earth with his impulse.
This Son of Strength, the upholder of Truth, has spread himself from afar like Sūrya with his radiance.

O King, worthy of sacrifice, you who are skillful in action, come to us; may Heaven, as it were, urge us toward complete attainment. Standing in his three abodes, he—like a conqueror, like a leaping steed—shall sacrifice the oblations and the riches of men. Whose impetuous flame, ruling over the forest, has shone forth like a goad that grows strong upon its path.
Deceitless like a swift runner, he perceives by himself; the immortal one, irresistible among the plants.
Agni Jātavedas is to be praised in our own home with our impetuous songs, like a steed that does not tire.
Winning booty through his power, like a horse, he has been made to grow old through sacrifices, like a father for his son.
Now they admire his splendors when he hews them out at will and follows along the broad earth;
he who, released and swift, runs instantly like a thief fleeing his debt across the desert wastes.
O steed, kindled with all thy fires, O Agni, protect us from reproach.
You come for wealth; you drive away misfortune. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
From you, O fortunate Agni, all blessings issue forth like branches from a tree.
Through obedience, there comes wealth, strength, and victory in the conquest of Vṛtra; there is the rain of heaven and the flow of waters, worthy of praise.
You are Bhaga for us, for you indeed bestow wealth; like one who traverses all, you dwell with wondrous splendor.
O Agni, like Mitra, you are the lord of the great *ṛta*, the distributor of abundant beauty, O God.
He, the lord of the good, slays Vṛtra with his might; O Agni, the inspired sage wins booty from the niggardly foe.
O wise one, born of Truth, whom you—being in harmony with the Son of Waters—urge forward with wealth;

That mortal who, O Son of Strength, has attained sharpening through his songs, hymns, and sacrifices known in the sacred knowledge— O God Agni, he receives every desirable thing as a boon; he possesses grain and rules over riches.
O Agni, Son of Strength, may you grant those men who possess great renown and heroic sons;

for by your power you provide abundant nourishment for cattle against the wolf and the predatory enemy. O Agni, Son of Strength, as a far-reaching speaker, grant us offspring and descendants who are victorious.
Through all my songs, may I attain abundance; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
The mortal who, through his thoughts and prayers, delights in the service of Agni—may he, enjoying prosperity, choose nourishment for his aid as of old.
For Agni here is indeed the wise one; Agni is the most skillful seer.
At the sacrifices, the human clans invoke Agni as the Hotṛ-priest.
For, O Agni, the wealth of the enemy vies with one another for your protection.
Overpowering the guileful Dasyus with their sacred rites, while seeking to overcome the lawless,
Agni bestows a hero who wins the waters, who endures the assault of enemies, and is the lord of the good.
At the mere sight of his might, his foes tremble in fear.
For Agni, by his wisdom, the god protects the mortal from reproach— he who is victorious,
whose wealth is never obstructed, and whose riches are ever-present in the contests for booty.
O you who are as vast as Mitra...
With my song, I adorn this guest of yours, who awakens at dawn, the lord of all the tribes.
By his very birth from heaven he seeks [the gods]; pure by nature, he eats for a long time that which is unshakable, even while still an embryo.
Him whom the Bhr̥gus established like a well-placed Mitra, the one to be praised, with upward-flaming radiance, within the tree.
O wondrous one, being well-pleased, you are magnified day by day with praises by Vītahavya.

As such, be the harmless increaser of Dakṣa’s power, the subduer of the enemy, whether distant or near. O Son of Strength, bestow upon mortals wealth and wide protection for Vītahavya; grant wide protection to Bharadvāja.
I strive toward your radiant guest, Agni, the son of heaven, the Hotṛ-priest of men who performs the sacrifice well—
toward him who, like a sage, possesses celestial speech, the bearer of oblations, the divine messenger,
with my well-fashioned hymns. He who, with his purifying and observant form, has shone upon the earth like the luster of the dawn.
RV 6.15.5: Like one who prevails on his journey, he is the joy of Etaśa; he who, like one parched by heat, is undecaying.
RV 6.15.6: Worship Agni after Agni with kindled fuel; praise your beloved guest, each one most dear to you.
Invite the Immortal with your songs; for as a god among gods, he wins what is desirable; for as a god among gods, he accepts our service.
I praise with song the kindled Agni, the pure, the purifier, the steadfast one at the forefront of the sacrifice;
the inspired priest, the invoker, the bountiful, the guileless sage—Jātavedas—we implore him with prayers for his favor.
Thee, O Agni, the immortal messenger, the bearer of oblations and the protector to be magnified, they have established in age after age.
Both gods and mortals have seated themselves with reverence before the watchful, all-pervading Lord of the People.
O Agni, adorning both worlds according to the sacred laws, you traverse the two realms as the messenger of the gods.
Since we choose your devotion and your favor, be therefore our auspicious protector, providing us with triple shelter.
Let us, who are ignorant, serve him who is of beautiful countenance, fair to behold, swift-moving, and more wise than the wise.
May he, knowing all ways, sacrifice; may Agni proclaim our oblation among the immortals. O Agni, you protect him and you bring him across, whoever has brought a prayer to you, a seer, O hero.
Whether it be the sharpening or the rising of the sacrifice, you fill that with power and with wealth.
O Agni, protect us from the one who seeks to harm us; O possessor of might, guard us from what is blameworthy.
May your path, accompanied by smoke, come together with us; may desirable wealth in the thousands gather around us.

Agni is the invoker, the lord of the household, the king; he, Jātavedas, knows all generations. He who is the most excellent sacrificer among both gods and mortals—let him, the upholder of *ṛta*, perform the sacrifice.
O Agni, O purifier, O bright-flamed one, you today serve as the invoker of the people at the sacrifice, for you are the true sacrificer.
Sacrifice according to the *ṛta* with your greatness, as you spread abroad; O most youthful one, carry the oblations that are yours today.
Look upon the well-placed offerings; may he establish you between the two worlds (*rodasī*) so that you may sacrifice.
Help us, O Bounteous One, in the winning of booty; O Agni, may we cross over all difficulties—may we cross them, may we cross them by your protection.
O Agni of the beautiful countenance, together with all the gods, sit first upon this wool-lined womb.
Lead the sacrifice, which is nest-like and rich in ghee, successfully to Savitṛ for the sake of the sacrificer.
Here, like Atharvan, the wise ones churn forth this very Agni.
Bringing hither Yama who hastens toward us, the unerring one from the dark shadows;
be born for the banquet of the gods, for complete well-being and prosperity. Bring the gods, the upholders of *ṛta*, who increase *ṛta*; let the sacrifice reach the gods.
O Agni, Lord of the House of men, we have made thee great with fuel.
May our household duties not be deficient; sharpen us with thy keen splendor.
O Agni, thou hast been appointed as the Hotṛ-priest of all sacrifices.
With the gods among the human race,
with your delightful tongues, do thou sacrifice for us at the rite to the Great One; bring hither the gods and worship them.
For you, O Ordainer, know straightway the ways and paths to the gods, O Agni of skillful wisdom, at our sacrifices.
Therefore, I praise you now as of old; may Bharata, with his prize-winning steeds, bring us prosperity.
He sacrificed at the sacrifice that reaches heaven. You [bestowed] these many desirable things for Divodāsa, who presses the soma, and for Bharadvāja, the donor.
As an immortal messenger, bring hither the divine folk,
listening to the well-spoken hymn of the sage. O Agni, mortal men with pious minds seek you, O God, for the feast.
At the sacrifices, they magnify the god. I worship your appearance and your will, O bounteous one;
may all who desire [you] take pleasure in them.
You are the Hotṛ priest appointed by Manu, the bearer of oblations, most wise through your mouth;
O Agni, worship the clans of heaven.
O Agni, come hither for the feast, being praised, to the giving of the sacrificial offering.
Sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacrificial grass.
O Aṅgiras, we strengthen you with fuel-sticks and with clarified butter; blaze forth brightly, O youngest one!
O God Agni, you win for us that fame which is wide and worthy of praise, and great heroic power.
From the lotus-leaf, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth.
[He is] the head of every priest.
The seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, kindled you,
the slayer of Vṛtra, the shatterer of forts.
Pāthya Vṛṣan kindled you, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the winner of wealth in every battle.
Come here; indeed, I shall speak these other songs to you, O Agni.
May you grow strong by these drops;
wherever you set your mind upon a higher skill,
there you shall make your seat.
For no one has ever surpassed your bounty, O Vasu, among those who bestow gifts; thus you shall accept our worship.
Agni, the son of Bharata, the slayer of Vṛtra, the one of many insights, has come hither.
The true lord of Divodāsa,
for he indeed bestows wealth upon all earthly beings by his greatness— conquering, unassailed, and invincible.
Like the ancients, O Agni, with your newest and enduring splendor,
you have spread far and wide with your lofty radiance.
O friends, boldly offer your hymn of praise and sacrifice to Agni.
And for the one who goes to the song, the ordainer—
for he indeed, throughout the ages of men, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest with the wisdom of a seer,
the messenger and the bearer of oblations.
O King, worship here those two sovereigns who observe pure vows— the Ādityas and the host of Maruts— and the two worlds,
O Vasu. O Agni, thy aspect is auspicious for the mortal who strives for nourishment.
To the Son of Strength, the Immortal—
may he grant us the best [gift] today through his wisdom. Seeking you with beautiful hymns, the mortal has attained [you] as one of noble splendor.

O Agni, those who are protected by you, seeking nourishment for their full span of life, overcome the hostilities of the enemy; they conquer the hostilities of the enemy. May Agni, with his sharp flame, strike down every devouring fiend.
Agni bestows wealth upon us.
O Jātavedas, you who are far-seeing, bring hither wealth with noble heroes;
slay the demons, O you of excellent wisdom!
O Jātavedas, protect us from distress and from the one who intends us evil; guard us, O Sage, through our sacred prayer (*brahman*).
O Agni, whatever mortal of evil intent offers us up to slaughter—
Therefore, protect us from distress. O God, with your tongue, drive away that evildoer—
the mortal who seeks to slay us.
O victorious Agni, grant wide-spreading protection to Bharadvāja; O Agni, bestow desirable wealth.
May Agni, seeking riches, strike down the Vṛtras with his song of praise.
Enkindled, bright, and offered with oblations;
In the womb of his mother, the father of the father, flashing within the imperishable,
he sits upon the seat of Ṛta.
O Jātavedas, O far-seeing one, bring us a prayer that wins progeny,
O Agni, which shines upon the heavens. O Son of Strength, those who offer sacrificial food draw near to you, whose appearance is delightful.
O Agni, we have released our songs;
like [seeking] shade from the heat of the sun, we have come for refuge under your protection, O Agni, you who are like gold in appearance.
Like a fierce archer, like a sharp-horned bull,
O Agni, you have shattered the fortresses. Him whom they carry like a ring-adorned hand, like a newborn infant.
Agni, the priest of the people, who performs the sacrifice well—
bring forth that god, the best finder of wealth, for the banquet of the gods;
let him sit down in his own place.
Sharpen the beloved guest who has been born within Jātavedas; settle him as the master of the house upon his pleasant seat.
O Agni, yoke those horses of yours, O God, which are well-trained.
They bear [thee] readily according to thy will. Come toward us;
bring [the gods] hither to enjoy the sacrificial offerings and to drink the Soma.
O Agni, descendant of Bharata, shine forth with undecaying splendor; blaze up and spread abroad, O ageless one!
The mortal who, desiring the feast, honors the god Agni and praises him at the sacrifice with an oblation—him [you favor].
With uplifted hands and with homage, one should seek to win the Hotṛ priest who sacrifices truly for both Heaven and Earth.
O Agni, we bring to you with a verse an oblation fashioned by our heart;
may these become for you bulls, stallions, and even barren cows.
The gods kindle Agni, the foremost, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, by whom wealth has been brought hither and the demonic powers shattered, O powerful one, worthy of sacrifice.
Drink the Soma, O mighty Indra, which you have sought; being praised, break open the great stall of cattle.

O bold one, wielder of the thunderbolt, you who with your might have slain Vṛtra and all hostile forces—protect him! O drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, victorious one, you who are the fair-cheeked bull of our prayers;
you who are the breaker of the cow-stalls, the wielder of the thunderbolt, and the one who stands upon the two bay horses—O Indra, pierce through to wondrous spoils of war!
Drink thus as of old; let it exhilarate you. Hear our prayer and grow strong through our songs of praise.
Make the sun manifest; cause the food to swell. Slay the enemies and pierce through for the cattle, O Indra.
These exhilarating draughts, O self-sustaining Indra, having been drunk, have made you, the radiant one, overflow with greatness.
The exhilarating [Soma-drops] have gladdened you, the great, the peerless, the powerful, the all-pervading, the subduer.
Intoxicated, with those [powers] you made the sun and the dawn shine forth, shattering even the firm fortresses.
O Indra, you shook the great mountain from its own place—the immovable one that held the cattle—driving them out from their secure dwelling.
By your wisdom and by your wondrous deeds, you have placed the ripe fruit within the raw cows through your power.
You threw open the doors for the ruddy cows; like a companion to the Aṅgirases, you released the cattle from the firm enclosure.
O Indra, you have filled the broad earth with your great might; lofty and sublime, you have propped up the high heaven.
Then you, O Indra, supported the two worlds, the parents of the gods, the ancient and mighty mothers of Eternal Order.
Then all the gods, O Indra, placed you alone, the powerful one, in the front for the battle;
when the godless one challenged the gods, they chose Indra here for the winning of the light of heaven.
Then even the heaven itself trembled at your thunderbolt, twice over, out of fear of its own fury,
when Indra, possessing all life, struck down the dragon who was seeking to devour him upon his couch.
And then, O fierce one, Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for you that great thunderbolt, with a thousand spikes and a hundred edges.

With that [Soma] which satisfies the heart's desire, you, O seeker of the residue, crushed the roaring Ahi. May all the Maruts, acting in harmony, increase for you, Indra, that [Soma] for which they cooked a hundred buffaloes.
Pūṣan and Viṣṇu caused the three lakes to flow for him, the slayer of Vṛtra, [to obtain] the exhilarating stalk.
You released the great, encompassed flood of the rivers, the obstructed wave of the waters.
Along their downward slopes, O Indra, you opened the path; the active streams flowed down toward the ocean.
Thus [we praise] Indra, who has performed all these deeds—the great, fierce, undecaying giver of victory.
May this new prayer turn you hither for our protection—you who possess noble heroes, excellent weapons, and a mighty thunderbolt.
O Indra, bestow upon us inspired singers glory, strength, nourishment, and radiant wealth.
O Indra, grant us heroic patrons among the Bharadvājas; and, O Indra, be mindful of us on the decisive day of battle.
Through this [prayer], may we win god-appointed booty; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
Praise him, Indra, who possesses overwhelming power, who conquers and is unassailed, the one invoked by many. Strengthen with these songs the invincible, fierce, and victorious bull of the people.
He is the warrior, the hero, the stirrer of battle, the one who shares the spoils, the great smasher, roaring like a bull, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*.
With his vast dust-clouds, the shaker of the human tribes, he alone has become the conqueror of the peoples.
Indeed, you alone, O unerring one, have subdued those Dasyus and protected the Aryan tribes.
Is this heroic power truly yours, O Indra? Or is it not yours? Declare it according to the truth.
For I believe that very power belongs to you, the one born with great might—the most victorious, the swifter than the swift.
It has become the fierce power of the fierce, the greater strength of the strong, the overcomer of the weak who is himself never weak.
May that ancient friendship of ours be with you, together with the Aṅgirases who speak thus;
O wonder-worker, shaker of the unshakable, you struck down Vala as he was fleeing, and you shattered all his fortresses and gates.
For he, the fierce one, is to be invoked with prayers as the lord-maker in the great battle against Vṛtra.
He, the wielder of the thunderbolt, became one who is to be invoked for the winning of offspring and progeny in battles;
he, by his greatness, has extended beyond the generations of men with his immortal name. He, the most heroic, dwells together with splendor, with power, with wealth, and with manly valor.
He who does not falter, whose people are never at variance, he of auspicious name— Indra shattered Cumuri and Dhuni,
Pipru, Śambara, and Śuṣṇa, for the sake of shattering forts and for eternal rest.
With uplifted power and most praiseworthy might, O Indra, mount your chariot for the slaying of Vṛtra.

Take the thunderbolt in your right hand; O bounteous one, shatter the magical illusions. Like Agni consuming a dry forest, O Indra, burn down the *rakṣas* with your weapon like a terrifying lightning bolt.
He who, with a deep and lofty [weapon], broke down the obstacles, drove away misfortunes, and struck them down.
O Indra of many glories, come hither by a thousand paths with wealth and with abundant strength,
O Son of Strength, you who, as the god invoked by many, alone rule over the granting of protection.
The greatness of the steadfast and impetuous one of many glories has surpassed both heaven and earth.
There is no enemy for him, no equal, and no standing ground for him, the one of many wiles and victorious might.
May that deed performed by you today be manifest: when you brought Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva to this man.
You sharpened many thousands against the earth; with boldness, you carried Tūrvayāṇ away.
Then, O God, all the gods rejoiced after you, the most wise among sages, when you, being praised,
created wide space for the oppressed heaven, for the people, and for yourself.
Heaven and Earth, and the immortal gods, yielded to that power of yours, O Indra.
O Doer of deeds, perform that which you have not yet done; through sacrifices, bring forth a new hymn of praise for yourself.
Great is Indra, manly, filling the people, and doubly vast, undiminished in his powers.
Turned toward us, he has increased his heroic might; broad and wide, he has been fashioned well by the makers.
The prayer has established Indra alone for the sake of winning booty—the great, the lofty, the ageless, the youthful—who, swelling with invincible power, has grown instantly to full perfection.
Widen your arms, extend your hands; mete out glories toward us.

Like a domestic herdsman driving his cattle to the herd, O Indra, turn us toward the prize in battle. We who long for strength shall now invoke that Indra of yours, the one who pervades with his powers, here and now. Just as the singers of old were—blameless, faultless, and unharmed.
Firm in his vows, giver of wealth, increased by Soma, he indeed possesses much desirable property.
Paths of riches meet in him, like rivers flowing together into the ocean.
O Hero, bring us most powerful strength; bring us the mightiest, overwhelming, and fierce power.
Bestow upon us all the splendors and manly powers of men, O Lord of Wealth, so that we may rejoice.

O Indra, bring to us that exhilaration of yours which is victorious in battle and never-failing, which has increased in strength; by means of which, when aided by you, we may think ourselves victors in the winning of offspring and progeny.
O Indra, bring us manly vigor that wins the prize, swelling and most skillful— by which, through your protections,
we may overcome our enemies in battles, whether they be kin or strangers. O Bull, let your vigor come to us from behind, from above, from below, and from the front.
Let them come together from every side; O Indra, bestow upon us splendor that reaches to heaven.
O Indra, may we win through your most heroic aids that which is desirable for men, along with glorious deeds.
For you, O King, behold the wealth of both worlds; bestow upon us a great, firm, and vast treasure.
[Bring] the bull accompanied by the Maruts...
O wielder of the thunderbolt, subject even that person who considers himself great to these men for whom I exist;
for we invoke you on earth in the struggle for heroes, for the sake of offspring, cattle, and waters.
O much-invoked one, through these friendships of yours, may we prevail over every enemy;
O hero, slaying both kinds of obstacles, may we rejoice in great wealth under your protection.
Like the sky, O Indra, that Aryan wealth stands overwhelming the people in battles by its might.

O Son of Strength, grant us that [Indra] who brings a thousandfold wealth, the winner of fertile lands, the overcomer of Vṛtra. To you, O Indra, all the power of the Asuras was entrusted by the gods, as it were from heaven— when you, O impetuous one, together with Viṣṇu, slew Ahi Vṛtra who had enclosed the waters.
Surpassing, more vigorous, and more powerful than the strong, Indra— whose greatness has increased through the performed *brahman*—
became the king of the honeyed Soma, when he came as the shatterer of all the fortresses.
By the hundreds, the Paṇis fled away there from Indra, for the sake of the ten-fingered sage, in the winning of the light.
With his weapons, he stripped away all the wiles of the insatiable Śuṣṇa; he left nothing remaining of him, as if of food.
All life was cast away from the great oppressor when Śuṣṇa fell at the stroke of the thunderbolt.
The Lord made wide room for his charioteer, Kutsa, on the same chariot, in the winning of the sun.
Like a hawk, he struck off the head of the Dāsa Namuci, churning up the intoxicating stalk for him.
He protected Namī Sāpya as he slept; may you fill us with wealth, with nourishment, and with well-being.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, by your might you shattered the strong fortresses of Pipru, who possessed the power of a serpent.
O Sudāman, you gave that imperishable wealth as a gift to the worshipper Ṛjiśvan. Indra, whose favor brings easy aid, [gave] Vetasu, who had ten fingers and was swift,
and he released Tugra Śaśvatibha to shine, so that he might approach his mother like a calf.
He, unopposed, overcomes his rivals, bearing in his hand the Vṛtra-slaying thunderbolt.
Standing upon his two bay steeds as if upon a chariot-seat, they carry the lofty Indra, yoked by our word.
O Indra, may we win through your newest protection; thus the Pūrus have praised you with sacrifices.
When you shattered the seven autumnal fortresses that provided refuge, you struck down the Dāsa cities to aid Purukutsa.
O Indra, you were the ancient increaser;
bestowing wealth upon Uśanas Kāvya, you gave away Navavāstva, who was not to be released, as his own grandson to his great father.
RV 6.20.12: O Indra, you are the shaker... RV 6.20.13: All that was yours in the battle, O Indra; Dhuni and Cumuri were laid low by your sleep.
Then Dabhīti, kindling the fuel, pressed the Soma for you, shining with his hymns of praise.
These invocations of the most frequent singer call upon you, O Hero, as one worthy of oblations.
The prayers, like wealth abundant and far-reaching, move with eloquence toward you, the ageless one who stands upon the chariot.
I shall praise that Indra, who is well-known, who is borne by songs, and who is magnified by hymns at the sacrifice.
Whose greatness exceeds that of heaven and earth, whose majesty overflows because of his manifold powers— He, indeed, made the pathless darkness possessed of paths by means of the sun.
O self-dependent one, when do mortals, seeking to worship, ever violate the ordinance of you, the immortal?
Where indeed is that Indra who performed those deeds? Among what people does he wander, and among which clans?
What sacrifice is pleasing to your mind and your desire? What is the hymn, O Indra, and who is that Hotar-priest?
For now, O doer of many deeds, these ancient friends of yours, born of old, have been active for you.
O you who are invoked by many, be mindful of those who are in the middle, as well as the recent ones, and even the most recent.

Inquiring about those ancient deeds of yours, O Indra, the later generations have followed after your glorious fame. O Hero, you to whom our prayers are brought, we praise you, the Great One, according to what we know of you.
The host of the Rakṣas has risen up against you, who were born with great power; stand firm against that!
With your ancient, allied friend, the thunderbolt, O bold one, drive away those who attack us.
But listen now, O Indra, to the prayer of the one who offers it, O hero, you who support the singer.
For you have been from of old the kinsman of our fathers, ever ready to be invoked in our quest.
Bring Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, and the Maruts to our aid for our protection today;
bring Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Agni, Purandhi, Savitṛ, the plants, and the mountains.
O you of many powers, O worthy of sacrifice, these singers here honor you with hymns.
Hear the call of those who invoke you; being invoked, there is no other like you, O Immortal One.
Now, O Son of Strength, come to my speech as one who knows, together with all the worshipful ones.

RV 6.21.11: Those who have Agni as their tongue, who honor the *ṛta*, who are of the nature of *asura*, and who made Manu superior to the Dasyu— RV 6.21.12: As such, be our leader on easy paths and on difficult ones, you who are the knower and the maker of the way. With those steeds that are unwearied, broad, and most capable of carrying, bring us, O Indra, toward booty.
I praise with these songs that Indra alone who is the one to be invoked by all people—
he who rules as the bull, possessed of virile power, the true hero, of many wondrous deeds, and mighty.
Him our ancient fathers, the Navagvas, the seven sages, impelled toward victory.

With hymns, we seek him who strikes down the one who strikes down, the overcomer who dwells upon the mountains, whose speech is guileless, and who is most powerful. We implore that Indra for this wealth which abounds in heroes, in men, and in much food—wealth that is unfailing, undecaying, and heavenly. O Lord of the Bay Steeds, bring that [wealth] so that we may rejoice.
Tell us that, O Indra, whether those who praised you in the past have indeed attained your favor.
What is your portion? What is your food, O fierce one, you who strike down, you who are invoked by many and possess much wealth, O slayer of the Asuras?
Now let this trembling, eloquent song go forth to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who stands upon his chariot—asking after him.
To him who seizes much, who performs many deeds, the giver of strength— [the worshipper] approaches the powerful one for the sake of the path and for nourishment.
O self-strong one, with this [bolt] sharpened by thought, which grows great through your own power,
you shattered even the unshakable, firm, and solid strongholds with boldness, O exuberant one.
Him, the most powerful one, the ancient, I would fain honor with a new prayer, as did the ancients.

May that Indra, the unassailable and excellent driver, carry us across all difficult passages. You have set ablaze the earthly, celestial, and intermediate regions for the sake of the person who acts with malice.

O Bull, burn them from every side with your flame; for the hater of sacred prayer, scorch him on earth and in the waters. You have become the king of the heavenly folk and of the earthly world, O you of brilliant aspect.
Grasp the thunderbolt in your right hand, O Indra; ageless one, you destroy all magical illusions.
O Indra, bring us restrained well-being, great and unfailing, for the overcoming of enemies—
that by which you, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, made the Dāsa and Ārya foes, and the Nahuṣa tribes, easy to overcome.
O much-invoked Ordainer, worthy of sacrifice, come to us with your teams of horses that bring all desirable things.
Neither the godless nor the god can restrain you; come quickly toward me with these [songs].
O Indra, you are closely united with the pressed soma, with the hymn of praise, with the sacred word (*brahman*), and with the recited chant (*uktha*).
Or whenever, O Maghavan, you go forth with your two harnessed bay steeds, O Indra, bearing the thunderbolt in your arms.
Whether you aided the presser in heaven at the decisive moment during the slaying of Vṛtra, O Indra, in the battle for heroes;
or whether, being yourself fearless, you subdued the defiant Dasyus while Dakṣa was afraid— O Indra,
may the fierce Indra be the drinker of the pressed Soma, leading the singer forward with his protection.
He makes space for the hero who presses the juice; he gives wealth even to the lowly singer who praises him.
He comes to the libations with his two bay steeds; bearing the thunderbolt, drinking the Soma, he bestows cattle.
He makes the hero manly, possessed of all heroes; he hears the call of the singer, borne by the hymns of praise.
Whatever he has achieved, that we offer to him—to Indra, who from of old has performed deeds for us.

When the Soma is pressed, we praise him with recitations and hymns, so that our prayer may be a source of strengthening for Indra. For you have made the prayers your means of growth; such as they are, O Indra, we serve you with our thoughts.

When the Soma is pressed, O drinker of the pressed juice, let us perform with sacrifices the most peaceful and delightful nourishments. As such, being pleased, take notice of our sacrificial cake; O Indra, drink the Soma mixed with milk.
Sit upon this sacrificial grass of the sacrificer; grant wide space for those who are devoted to you.
Rejoice indeed according to your pleasure, O fierce one; may these sacrifices reach you.
May these invocations reach you, the much-invoked one, among us; toward you, O Indra, this prayer of ours goes forth, seeking wealth.
O friends, as you do at the libations, fill that generous Indra with Soma juices.
RV 6.23.9: Will Indra not surely grant us aid for the sake of this gift, nor neglect the presser of the Soma?

RV 6.23.10: Thus has Indra been praised while the Soma was pressed among the Bharadvājas, he who dwells among the wealthy patrons. May Indra be the giver of wealth containing all desirable things to the singer and to the patron.
The bull-like exhilaration, the hymn, and the songs of praise are with Indra, who drinks the pressed soma, the consumer of the dregs.
The bounteous Maghavan, worthy of praise by men through their hymns, is the king dwelling in heaven whose protection is imperishable.
He is the victorious hero, manly and discerning; he hears the call of the singer and extends his wide-reaching aid.
The Vasu, the one praised by men, the sustainer of the singer, the prize-winner, when lauded in the assembly, bestows the prize.
Like the axle of two wheels, O Hero, your greatness exceeds the two worlds in its vastness.
O Indra, invoked by many, like the branches of a tree, your many outstretched arms have grown forth.
O Lord of Śacī, you of many powers, your powers are like the paths for driving cattle;
they are like the cords for calves, O Indra—both bound and unbound, O Bounteous Giver.
One deed Indra performs today, another tomorrow; he makes the non-existent and the existent appear in an instant.
In this matter, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Pūṣan are our noble guardians who direct our will.
From you, O Indra, they brought forth the waters with hymns and sacrifices, as if from the back of a mountain.
Seeking booty, those who carry songs to you have come toward you with these fair praises, like horses to a race.
Neither autumns nor months, nor days, wear Indra out; they do not diminish him.
Though he is already grown, let his body increase as it is celebrated with hymns and recited praises.
When praised, he does not bow before the strong, nor the firm, nor the arrogant one incited by the Dasyus.
Even the level plains and the lofty mountains are but a ford for Indra; even in the deep he finds a bottom.
O Amatri, drinker of the pressed juice, bestow upon us strength through your wide and deep protection.
Stand up erect with your aid, remaining unharmed at the dawning of night during the final watch.
Be present for our protection in the encounter; O Indra, protect him from harm here.
Protect him at home and in the forest from harm; may we rejoice for a hundred winters with brave sons.
O mighty Indra, whatever aid you have—whether it be the lowest, the highest, or that which is in the middle—[is yours].
With these [helps] and with these strengths, O mighty and fierce one, you have indeed protected us in the slaying of Vṛtra.
With these, O Indra, warding off harm, you have confounded the fury of the enemy as he strove against contending rivals.
With these, you have cast down all the attacking Dāsa tribes in every direction for the sake of the Ārya.
O Indra, those who have joined as attackers—whether they be kin or strangers—turning their chariots hitherward;
do thou strike down their wavering strength, destroy their manly powers, and drive them away.
Or rather, the hero overcomes the hero with his body when they both strive for victory, each shining with his own form as they struggle.

Whether for offspring, cattle, or progeny, or when the two armies cry out against one another over waters or fertile fields—no hero, no swift one, no bold man, nor any warrior thinking himself such, has ever fought against you. O Indra, no one stands as your equal; you surpass all these created beings.
He rules over both kinds of manly power when the wise ones call upon him in the assembly;

whether against the great Vṛtra or in a dwelling rich in heroes, whenever the two sides, wide-expanding, stretch out their forces. And then, O Indra, when the people stir, be a savior and a protector.
RV 6.25.7: Those of ours who are most heroic, O Indra, our noble patrons, have placed us before them.
RV 6.25.8: To you was granted for your great Indra-power all at once; it followed you in every Vṛtra-slaying.
It followed your dominion, your conquering might, O worshipful Indra, and with the gods it followed you in the subduing of men.
RV 6.25.9: Thus bring our rivals together in battles; O Indra, take pleasure in the contending godless hosts.
May we, the Bharadvājas, singing your praises, find your protection at the break of day, even now, O Indra.
RV 6.26.1: Hear us, O Indra! We invoke you, raining down blessings, for the winning of great booty.
When the clans gathered together for the battle of heroes, grant us fierce protection on the decisive day.
The prize-winning son of a prize-winner calls upon you for the winning of great booty that may be seized.
Indra, the lord of the virtuous, the deliverer, you he looks to in the midst of Vṛtras; the boxer looks to you as he fights for cattle.

You urged on the seer in the winning of the sun; you struck down Śuṣṇa for the sake of the worshipper Kutsa. You struck off the head of the invulnerable one, intending to perform a deed worthy of praise for Atithigva.
You brought forward the lofty chariot and the warrior; you protected the fighting bull Daśadyu.
You slew Tugra together with Vetasu; O Indra, you protected Tuji when he was chanting your praises.
O Indra, you performed that great deed through your power; O Hero, you shattered thousands.
You struck down the Dāsa Śambara from the mountain and protected Divodāsa with your wondrous aids.
Rejoicing in the acts of faith and in the Soma juices, O Indra, you sent Cumuri to sleep for Dabhīti.
Bestowing favor upon Piṭhīnas, you struck down sixty thousand Rajis together with your skillful power. May I, along with the patrons, attain that superior bliss and strength of yours, O Indra.
When, O most powerful one, heroes praise you with their threefold protection, O possessor of true heroes, like the Nahuṣas;
may we, O Indra, be your dearest friends in this invocation for glory, through your greatness.
May Prātardani be the foremost, glorious in sovereignty, in the slaying of Vṛtras and in the winning of riches.
In what did Indra take pleasure during its exhilaration, or what did he do upon drinking it? What did he accomplish in its friendship?
Or were those delights found by him in the past when it was present, or what [did he find] in its newer forms?
In its exhilaration, Indra performed what is good; upon drinking it, he performed what is good; in its friendship, he performed what is good.
Those who were present at his revelry when he sat down have found his ancient and even his newest riches.
For we do not know the measure of your entire greatness, O Maghavan, nor your wealthiness;
nor have we ever seen the full extent of your power, O Indra, in every new gift you bestow.
This very power of yours was recognized, by which you struck down the offspring of Varaśikha.
O Indra, when your thunderbolt was hurled, it shattered even the mountain from its forceful roar.
Indra slew the offspring of Varaśikha, bestowing aid upon Abhyāvartin as he sought his favor.
When you struck down Vṛcīvat on the Hariyūpīyā river, the one in the front fled in fear while the other remained.
O Indra, much-invoked, three thousand armored men together with their wives fell upon the Yavyāvatī in their desire for glory;
the Vṛcīvats, falling before your arrow, went to their destruction like shattered vessels.
He whose two ruddy bulls, seeking good pasture, move between the two poles licking their lips—
he, bestowing Turvaśa upon Sṛñjaya, gave Vṛcīvan to Daivavāta,
providing for him. O Agni, the liberal sovereign Maghavan has given me forty chariot-drawing horses and stallions with mares.
Turning hitherward and hastening, this difficult-to-attain sacrificial fee of the Pārthavas is bestowed.
The cows have come; they have performed what is auspicious. Let them sit in the cow-pen and take delight with us.
May they be here, prolific and many-formed, yielding their milk for Indra through many dawns.
Indra bestows gifts upon the one who sacrifices and the one who gives; he grants them and does not steal back what is his own.
Increasing his wealth more and more, he places the god-fearing man upon an unbroken field of land.
These [gifts] do not perish; no thief can harm them, nor can the enemy’s distress overcome them.
With those [cows] by which one worships the gods and gives gifts, the lord of cattle dwells for a long time together with them.
The dust-raising, hoof-beating steed does not overtake them; they do not go toward the place of slaughter. Far-striding and fearless, those cows roam about following that mortal who is a sacrificer.
The cows are Bhaga; the cows have appeared to me as Indra; the cows are the first draught of Soma.
O people, these are the cows; with my heart and mind I truly desire Indra.
O cows, you make even the emaciated fat, and you make even the unlovely beautiful of countenance.
Make our home auspicious, O you of auspicious speech; great strength is proclaimed for you in the assemblies.
May they be rich in offspring, grazing on good pasture, drinking pure waters at excellent watering-places. Let not the thief nor the malevolent man master you; may the missile of Rudra avoid you.

Let this mixture be poured into these cows; let it be mixed with the seed of the bull, O Indra, and with your own heroic power. The men have sought Indra for friendship, going toward him as they desire his great favor.
For he, the great giver with the thunderbolt in his hand, exists; worship him, the great and joyous one, for protection.
In whose hand men have placed their strength, who stands upon the golden chariot as its lord— the reins are upon his firm arms, and the stallions are yoked on the path like bulls.
For the sake of glory, the feet have been anointed for thee; bold wielder of the thunderbolt, thou art rich in strength and gifts.
Clothed in a fragrant robe, beautiful to behold, thou hast become powerful like the sun, O dancer.
That Soma has been pressed most thoroughly mixed, in which the cooked offering and the grains are prepared.
The men, praising Indra, performing sacred prayers, and reciting hymns, are most beloved by the gods.
No limit can be set to your power; indeed, you have pushed apart heaven and earth with your greatness.
The patron, hastening with his aid, bestows these gifts, gathering them together like herds in the waters.
Thus indeed is Indra, the great one, easy to invoke; he is the one who responds with or without being called, the golden-jawed warrior.
For even as soon as he was born, he possessed unequalled strength; he slays many Vṛtras and strikes down the Dasyus.
He has increased all the more for heroic deeds; alone and ageless, he distributes riches.
Indra has surpassed heaven and earth; indeed, he exceeds both the worlds. Therefore, I consider his divine power to be vast; no one can diminish those things which he has established.
Day after day, the sun has become visible; the one of noble wisdom has widely laid out the dwellings.
Even now, indeed, that work of the rivers remains as it was when you, O Indra, dug out a path for them.
The mountains settled down like guests at a feast; by you, O wise one, the firm regions were established.
Truly this is so: there is no other like you, O Indra—neither god nor mortal is greater.
You slew the serpent as he lay encompassing the flood; you released the waters toward the ocean.
O Indra, you threw open the waters in all directions and shattered the firm stronghold of the mountain.
You became the king of the moving world and of the peoples, bringing forth the sun, the sky, and the dawn together.
O Lord of wealth, you alone have become the master of riches; O Indra, you have placed the peoples within your hands.
For the sake of offspring, of waters, of progeny, and of the sun, the people with their various voices have raised their cries.
Out of fear of you, O Indra, all the earthly realms—even those that are unshakable—cause the regions to tremble.
Heaven and earth, the mountains, and the forests—all that is firm trembles at your onset.
O Indra, with Kutsa you fought against the insatiable Śuṣṇa and Kuyava in the quest for cattle.
At the onset of the sun, you stole the wheel; you have warded off the sins.

You struck down the hundreds of unassailable fortresses of Śambara; you, O powerful one, bestowed riches with your might upon Divodāsa when he pressed the juice, and upon the praising Bharadvāja when he prepared the soma.
O hero of true valor, O possessor of great manly strength, mount your terrible chariot for the sake of the great battle.
Come along the distant paths, O helper, toward me; being renowned, make yourself heard among all people.

For this great hero, the powerful and swift one, I have fashioned with my mouth most ancient and most abundant words—most auspicious words—for the exuberant wielder of the thunderbolt, the steadfast one.
He, being praised by the wise, caused the two parents to dwell with the sun; he shattered the mountain while being lauded.
Bellowing with the well-intentioned singers, he released the confinement of the ruddy cows.
With his priests, the singers who were steadfast in their purpose, he, the doer of many deeds, repeatedly won the cattle.
Striking down citadel after citadel with his friends, he, being himself a seer, shattered the strongholds with his seers.
O Bull of the peoples, lover of songs, come forth for our well-being with your girdled throngs, with great spoils, and with mighty strengths, accompanied by many heroes.
Impelled by his own impetuous might, Indra, the swift conqueror, has with his steeds driven the waters to the right.
Thus released, they have flowed day after day for the sake of the goal, irresistible and unrestrained.
O Indra, grant us that most powerful exhilaration which is heroic, most victorious, and bountiful.
He who possesses good horses shall win the prize of noble steeds; he shall overcome the Vṛtras and his enemies in battles.
For indeed, O Indra, the peoples with contending voices invoke you for protection in the struggle for heroes.
You, with the inspired singers, have struck down the Paṇis; protected by you, the steed wins the prize of booty.
O Heroic Indra, you have slain both kinds of enemies—the Dāsa and the Ārya foes—like trees with well-aimed arrows; O most manly one, you rend them in battle among men.
As such, O Indra, be our friend with your unerring protections, a guardian for all our life, and a promoter of our growth.
When we call upon you for the winning of the light, O Hero, as we fight in the battles for the prize of the herd;

now, O Indra, be ours for the future as well—be gracious to us and our protectors. Thus praising, under the protection of the Mighty One, may we be at the decisive moment, most successful in winning cattle.
Many songs have come together unto you, O Indra, and from you proceed manifold thoughts.
The praises of the seers, both ancient and recent, and their hymns and chants, have vied with one another for Indra’s favor.
He who is invoked by many, praised by many, the skillful one, alone is glorified by many through sacrifices.
Like a chariot harnessed for great power, Indra has become one to be celebrated by us in song. Neither prayers nor hymns harm him; reaching Indra, they cause him to grow strong.
Whether a hundred or a thousand singers praise him who delights in songs, all that is well for him.
For him, as for the heavenly light, the months have poured forth; the Soma has been offered into Indra.
When the waters gathered together like people in a desert, they strengthened his invocations through sacrifices.
For him, this great song of praise; for Indra, this hymn has been spoken with inspired thoughts.
As it was not so in the great battle against Vṛtra, may Indra, the life-sustainer of all, be our protector and our strengthener.
When shall our sacred prayers find their rest in the chariot? When will you grant the singer nourishment for a thousandfold prosperity?
When will you clothe this hymn with wealth? When will you make our thoughts rich with the prize of booty?
RV 6.35.2: When indeed will that happen, O Indra, when you, with men, shall settle men; with heroes, heroes; and with victory, conquer the adversaries? RV 6.35.2:
You shall win the threefold cattle among the herds; O Indra, bestow upon us glory together with the sun. RV 6.35.3:
When indeed will that happen, O most powerful Indra, when you shall make the prayer effective for the singer throughout all waters?
When will you yoke your thoughts like teams of horses? When will you come to the invocations rich in cattle?

Bestow upon the singer, O Indra, gifts of cattle, horses, and golden splendor, and food renowned for its strength. Make the cow swell with milk that is easy to milk; shine forth with great luster among the Bharadvājas.
Now, O Śakra, you are truly a hero in that you open up the enclosure, even though it is otherwise difficult to enter.
Do not let the cow who milks out the bright [soma] go away; O Sage, quicken the Aṅgirases with our prayer.
Truly, your exhilarations are for all people, and truly so are the riches that belong to the earth.
You have always been the distributor of spoils of war, since you have maintained divine power among the gods.
The people have followed his strength; they have fully entrusted their vigor to him for heroic deeds.
Even in the slaying of Vṛtra, they direct their will toward the snare-grasper, the fierce one, and the steed.
To him, the converging aids, manly powers, and strengths have followed Indra;
like rivers to the ocean, our songs—impetuous with hymns—enter him who is wide-expansive.
Being praised, release for us a spring of wealth, O Indra, of thy riches that shine manifold.
You have become the peerless lord of men, the sole king of the entire world.
As such, hear us with your hearing, you who are worthy of worship; like the sky over the earth, you are the master of wealth beyond our reach.
May you, being pleased by our power, be manifest to us through our strength in age after age.
O fierce Indra, let your harnessed bay horses bring your chariot, which possesses all treasures, hitherward.
For even the poor man invokes you, O possessor of heaven; may we prosper today at your shared banquet.
The bay horses have gone forth to their work at the wooden vat; being purified, they have become straight-moving.
May Indra, our ancient one, drink first of this; may the heavenly King drink of the exhilarating Soma.
Like chariot-horses on well-wheeled wheels, let them carry the powerful Indra toward us with speed, rushing toward glory. Now indeed, the nectar of Vāyu shall never fail.
Most excellent, Indra, the most active among the wealthy patrons,
sets his sacrificial fee in motion— by which, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you ward off distress and, O bold one,
bestow riches upon the wise singers. May Indra, the giver of enduring strength, may he whose greatness has increased, be magnified by our songs.
May Indra be the most effective slayer of Vṛtra; as a hero, he, the patron, bestows gifts with vigorous haste.
From here, let the most wondrous one come to us; may he bear up our great and glorious invocation of Indra.
On the path of the divine host, the bounteous giver wins praise-worthy prayer and the gift of the people.
Even from afar, his ears hear; speaking aloud, he makes his voice heard like the thundering of Indra.

May this invocation of the gods bring him hither; may this recited hymn turn Indra toward me. With my highest devotion, I have celebrated with songs that Indra, the ancient-born and undecaying, for you.
The sacred prayers have been offered together in him; may the great hymn of praise increase Indra.
May the sacrifice and Soma strengthen Indra; may the prayer, the songs, the recitations, and the meditations strengthen him.
May the dawns at their rising strengthen him; may the nights, the months, the autumns, and the days strengthen Indra.
Thus, him who was born for complete power, who has grown strong for renowned bounty—
O sage, let us now indeed summon that great and fierce one for our protection in the battles against Vṛtra.
Of the exhilarating, wise, divine bearer, the inspired thought of the sweet speech.
O God, bestow upon us that wealth which is shared among the gods; grant it to the singer, preceded by cattle.
Desiring this, he has gone around the mountain with those whose thoughts are fixed on *ṛta*, yoking himself with those joined to *ṛta*.
Indra broke the unbroken ridge of Vala; with his words, he fought against the Paṇis.
This Indu, O Indra, has illuminated the days with light, through the nights and dawns, throughout the autumns.
They have established him as the banner of these days; he has made the Dawns shine with pure birth.
Illuminating the unlit, he has shone forth; by means of the Eternal Law (ṛta), he has clothed the many ancient ones.

He has been brought hither by the steeds yoked in accordance with Truth, finding the light of heaven with his central nave, filling the people. Now, O ancient King, being praised, swell abundant nourishments for the singer, for the granting of wealth.
Grant waters, non-poisonous plants, forests, cattle, horses, and men for the sake of hymnic praise.
O Indra, drink! The juice is pressed for you, for intoxication. Unharness your two bay steeds, O friend.
And sing forth, sitting down with the host; then bestow vigor upon the singer for the sacrifice.
Drink of this, O Indra, of which you drank at your birth for exhilaration and for wisdom, O mighty one.
The cows, the men, the waters, and the pressing-stone have brought that *indu* of yours together for him to drink.
When the fire is kindled and the Soma is pressed, O Indra, let your bay steeds, most capable of carrying you, bring you hither.
With a mind directed toward you, I call upon you repeatedly; O Indra, come for our great prosperity.
Come hither; you have always come at our longing, O Indra, with your great mind to the drinking of the Soma. Listen to these our prayers, and then let the sacrifice bestow vigor upon your body.
Whether you are in heaven on the decisive day, or apart from that, or in your own dwelling, wherever you may be—come!
Therefore, with your team of horses, come to our sacrifice for our protection; being of one mind with the Maruts, O lover of songs, drink [the soma].
Without anger, come to the sacrifice; for you the pressed drops flow clear. O wielder of the thunderbolt, like cows to their own stall, O Indra, come as the first among those worthy of worship.
That well-formed, most excellent palate of yours, with which you ever drink the wave of honeyed mead—with that, drink!
The Adhvaryu has stepped forward for you; O Indra, let your thunderbolt, seeking cattle, turn toward you.
This drop, the bull of every form, the Soma, has been prepared for Indra, the bull.
Drink this, O Lord of Bay Horses, fierce driver, over whom you have presided from of old; this is your food.
The pressed Soma, O Indra, is better than the unpressed; it is more excellent for the wise one’s delight. O Conqueror, come to this sacrifice; with it, fill yourself full of all your powers.
We call upon you, O Indra; come hither! Let the Soma be sufficient for your body, O Śatakratu. Rejoice in the pressed juices; protect us in battles and among our people.
Bring all things to this one who desires to drink, he who knows all.
To him who comes readily, who moves swiftly, the hero who never lags behind—
to him come forth with Soma juices, for he is the greatest drinker of Soma;
with vessels full of the dregs, with pressed drops, [honor] Indra, the possessor of the *ṛjīṣa*.
If you honor him with the pressed drops, with the Soma juices—the wise one knows all; boldly he seeks each and every one of them.
O Adhvaryu, bring forth the pressed juice for this very person, for this very person, from the plant.
Would he not protect us from the curse of the common, arrogant kinsman?
In whose exhilaration you delivered Śambara to Divodāsa— This is that Soma pressed for you, O Indra; drink!
Whose sharp-pressed exhilarating drink you guard at its beginning, middle, and end—
this is he...
In whose exhilaration you released the cows that were held fast within the rocks.
He, being exhilarated by the soma-juice, has assumed the power of Maghavan.
RV 6.43.4.2: This is he...
He who is the wealthiest among the wealthy, who is most resplendent in splendors—
O Indra, Lord of the *svadhā*, this pressed Soma is your intoxicating draught. It is that which is powerful for you, O Most Powerful One, the giver of riches and of inspired thoughts.
The pressed Soma...
[is he] by whom the one who has grown great is not surpassed in might, nor the swift one in his own aids.
The pressed Soma...
I praise this one for you, the unassailable lord of power,
Indra, the all-conquering hero, the most bountiful, who belongs to all people. Him whom these songs magnify— the lord of swift bounty.
The two divine worlds, Heaven and Earth, revere that very strength of his.
This is the expansion of your hymn, intended to spread out as a seat for Indra—
for him whose aids, like inspired songs, grow forth together from their common dwelling.

Mitra, the most recent one, has found skill; having drunk, he has brought forth better wealth for the gods. Having won with the *staulā* and *dhautarī* dice, he became a wide protector for his friends.
On the path of Truth, the wise one has been drunk; the gods have set their minds upon glory.
Assuming a great name through his words, the beloved one has revealed his form for all to see.
Bestow upon us most brilliant skill; ward off the many hostilities of men.
Grant us more abundant vitality through your powers; aid us in the winning of wealth.
O Indra, O Maghavan, we have become yours; O Lord of Bay Horses, do not turn away from us as our giver.
No kinsman is seen among mortals—why then, indeed, do they call you the one who impels the weak?
O Bull, do not abandon us to exhaustion; let us not suffer harm in the friendship of you, the wealthy one.
Many are your restraints among men, O Indra; slay those who do not press the Soma, root out those who give no gifts.
Like thundering clouds releasing water, Indra pours forth riches of horses and kine.
From of old you have been the sustainer of the singer; let not the stingy misers deceive you, O Maghavan.
O hero, Adhvaryu, bring the pressed juices to the great Indra; for he is the king thereof.
He who has grown strong through the ancient and the new songs of the praising seers.
In his exhilaration, Indra, knowing many forms, struck down the Vṛtras that were irresistible.
Offer this honeyed Soma to him, to the hero with the handsome jaws, so that he may drink it.
May Indra be the drinker of the pressed Soma; exhilarated, may he slay Vṛtra with his thunderbolt.
May he come even from afar to the sacrifice, the Vasu who protects our prayers and sustains the singer.
This is that very vessel for Indra’s drinking; Indra’s beloved nectar has been drunk. May it exhilarate the god for his goodwill, and may it drive away from us hatred and distress.
Rejoicing in this, O Hero, slay the enemies—the kinsmen and the strangers, O Maghavan—those who are our adversaries.
O Indra, crush and slay those who advance with their armies against us from every direction.
O Maghavan Indra, in these battles of ours, grant us great freedom and a path easy to traverse.
For the winning of waters, of offspring, and of progeny, O Indra, place our patrons on your side.

Let the bay steeds, the vigorous ones, being harnessed—horses with powerful chariots and powerful reins—come toward us. Let the vigorous steeds, the carriers of the thunderbolt, well-yoked, bring you here for the sake of the vigorous exhilaration.
O vigorous one, your vigorous [steeds] have reached the vat, dripping with clarity like waves exulting.
O Indra, for you, the bull, the strong ones bring the pressed soma; to you, the vigorous bull, they offer the soma.
You are the bull of heaven, the bull of earth; you are the bull of the rivers, the bull of the moving creatures.
For you, the vigorous bull, the drop has swelled—the sweet juice, the honeyed draught, for your choice.
This god, being born with might, together with Indra as his ally, paralyzed Paṇi.
This Indu stole away the weapons from his own father and the magic powers of the malevolent one. He made the dawns have good husbands; he placed light within the sun.
He found the hidden nectar in the three realms within the luminous spheres of heaven, in the three places. He propped apart heaven and earth; he yoked the chariot with its seven reins.
By his power, Soma placed the cooked milk within the cows and sustained the fountain with its ten mechanisms.
Indra, our youthful friend, who by his excellent guidance brought Turvaśa and Yadu from afar—
may he bestow vigor even upon the uninspired and speed even upon the slow horse.
Indra is the conqueror who bestows wealth;
great are his guidances, and many indeed are his praises; his aids never fail.
O friends, sing praises and chant aloud for him who is borne by the sacred word (*brahma*); for he is our great protector.
O slayer of Vṛtra, you are the guardian of one, and you are the guardian of two.
And such as we are, you lead us;
you drive away our enemies and make us reciters of hymns.
O hero among men, you are called "the one with noble sons."
With hymns, I call upon the Brahman, the bearer of the sacred word, the friend worthy of praise,
as one calls a cow to be milked.
In whose two hands they say all treasures are deposited from of old.
Of the hero who conquers armies; O wielder of the stone, O Lord of Might, unbending one, tear asunder the strongholds and the magic spells of men.
We, desiring glory, have invoked you, O Indra, true drinker of Soma, Lord of spoils. We have invoked you,
who were there in the past, or who are now present when the prize is set.
Worthy of invocation, hear our call!
O Indra, with our prayers and swift steeds,
may we win through you the prize-winning horses and the wealth placed as a stake.
O Hero, lover of songs, you have become great, O Indra, when the prize is set; you are to be sought in the battle for booty.
O Slayer of Foes, let that aid of yours which is most swift in its impulse be present.
With that [chariot], urge our chariot forward. As the best of charioteers with this chariot of ours, which is ready for battle, may you, O Victor, win the wealth set before us.
