Praise him who is the one and only, the observer of all people among the tribes;
he was born as the Lord of men, possessing manly power.
He who has been a friend to those who sing his praises, a gracious companion through his protection.
As such, O Indra, have mercy upon us!
Take up the thunderbolt in your hands for the slaying of the Rākṣasas, O wielder of the bolt; may you utterly conquer our adversaries.
I invoke the ancient friend, the companion of riches, the inciter of the poor, who is most frequently invoked with sacred prayers;
for he alone rules over all earthly treasures.
O most beloved of song,
O irresistible one, fulfill our desire with teams of horses, with riches consisting of horses, and with cattle, O bold lord of cattle!
Sing that song for you at the libation, for the one invoked by many, the warrior,
which is as beneficial as it is for a powerful bull.
The Vasu indeed does not withhold the gift of wealth consisting of cattle,
when he has heard our songs.
May the slayer of Dasyus surely go to his cow-filled stall.
With your powers, open up for us.
O Śatakratu, these songs have cried out to you,
as mother cows low to their calf, O Indra.
Your friendship is difficult to attain; you are a bull for one who desires cattle, O hero;
be a horse for one who desires horses. Rejoice indeed in the soma-juice...
O lover of songs, at every pressing these hymns reach you,
as milch-cows low toward their calf.
You are the most frequent guest in the many voices of the numerous worshippers.
With strengths, for those seeking strength—
O Indra, may our hymn of praise be most effective and closest to you;
impel us toward great wealth.
Bṛbu has taken his stand upon the highest head of the Paṇis,
like the broad forest-thicket on the banks of the Gaṅgā;
he whose auspicious gift flows swiftly like the wind is thousandfold.
Immediately he bestows great gifts.
Therefore, all our noble singers always praise him:
Bṛbu, the most liberal giver of thousands, the patron who wins thousands most abundantly.
For we poets indeed call upon you for the winning of booty;
O Indra, lord of the virtuous, men call upon you in battles against the Dasyus, and you, who possess the sun, in the races toward the goal.
Therefore, O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, when you are praised as the great one, O lord of the stones, act with boldness on our behalf.
O Indra, bestow upon us cattle and chariot-horses; pour forth wealth entirely for us, as if for a victor.
We invoke that Indra who is the all-conquering, far-seeing one. O Lord of heroes, with a thousand testicles and great manly vigor, be our strengthener in battles.
You strike down men with wrath like a bull, O impetuous one, bounteous giver, worthy of praise. Be our protector in the great contest for wealth, for our bodies, for the waters, and for the sun.
O Indra, bring us the highest, most powerful, and fulfilling fame.
O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, fair-cheeked god, by whom you have filled both these worlds, heaven and earth;
we invoke you, the fierce one who subdues the peoples, O King among the gods, for our protection.
O Vasu, make all our wavering things firm, and make our enemies easy to overcome.
O Indra, whatever vigor and manly strength you have bestowed upon the Nahuṣa tribes,
or whatever splendor belongs to the five peoples— bring all those heroic powers hither at once.
Or whatever virile power you have in Tr̥kṣi, O Maghavan, among the Druhyus, or among the Pūrus— [bring that too].
Bestow that upon us for the conquest of men, for the overcoming of enemies in battle.
O Indra, grant a threefold shelter, a triple-protecting refuge full of well-being; bestow this protection upon the liberal patrons and upon me, and turn away the missile from them.
Those who, with minds intent on cattle, have overcome the enemy, strike him down boldly.
O Indra, Maghavan, lover of songs, be our closest protector of our bodies.
And now, O Indra, be for our prosperity; do not abandon us in battle.
When the winged thunderbolts with sharpened points fly through the mid-air;
where the heroes extend their bodies and find the dear protection of the fathers— then grant us and our offspring a secure shelter, and drive away the unseen enmity.
When, O Indra, you urge on the coursers in the release for the great prize,
upon the uneven road and the crooked path like falcons seeking glory;
when you speed them like rivers down a slope, even if you must roar along with the toil.

They who, like birds, wheel about when seized by the arms for the sake of the prize in the contest for cattle—this [Soma] is indeed sweet, it is honeyed; this is indeed strong, it is full of flavor. And truly, no one at all could withstand Indra in battles after he has drunk of this.
This sweet juice has been most intoxicating here, by which Indra was exhilarated in the slaying of Vṛtra.
It is this which destroyed the many great deeds of Śambara and his ninety-nine fortresses. This, when drunk, stirs up my voice; this has awakened my longing wisdom.
This wise one measured out the six wide expanses, from which no being whatsoever is excluded. He is he who created the breadth of the earth and the height of heaven;
he established the nectar in the three floods and Soma in the broad mid-air.
He has found the wondrous vision, the ocean, at the forefront of the dawns in the bright abode.
This great one, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, has propped up the sky with a mighty pillar.
Drink boldly the Soma from the beaker, O Indra, hero and slayer of Vṛtra, in the battle for riches.
At the midday libation, pour forth; as the abode of wealth, bestow wealth upon us.
O Indra, look out for us like a leader; lead us further toward greater prosperity.
Be a good ferryman who carries us across; be a good guide and a gracious leader.
O Knower, lead us to wide space; lead us to the light of heaven, free from fear, to well-being.
High and mighty are your arms, O Indra, you the steadfast; may we find refuge beneath them, vast and secure.
Place us, O Indra, upon the broadest seat of your chariot, drawn by your two most swift horses, O Lord of a hundred powers.
Bring us nourishment, the most excellent of all nourishments; O Maghavan, let not the wealth of the enemy bypass us.
O Indra, be gracious; desire life for me and sharpen my prayer like the edge of iron.
Whatever I, devoted to you, speak here—be pleased with that and make me one who possesses the gods.
I invoke Indra, the protector; Indra, the helper; at every call, the hero Indra who is easy to invoke.
I call upon Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many; may the bounteous Indra grant us well-being.
May Indra, the excellent deliverer, the possessor of wealth, through his aids, be gracious, he who is all-knowing.
May he drive away hatred and grant us fearlessness; may we be masters of heroic power.
May we abide in the favor of that one worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious goodwill.
May that Indra, the good protector and possessor of wealth, drive our enemies far away from us.
O Indra, as waves rush down a slope, so do our songs, prayers, and teams of horses speed toward you.
Like vast wealth, you gather for yourself many libations, waters, cows, and Soma drops, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
Who shall praise him? Who shall satisfy him? Who shall sacrifice to him, since the bountiful Lord always protects the fierce one?
Striking them as if with his feet, he makes one after another—first and then the next—by his powers. The hero is heard to be fierce against the fierce, subduing one and leading another away;
Indra, the king of both worlds, whose hatred increases, overcomes the people and men.
He casts aside his friendships with the former ones; hurrying forward, he goes with others.
Shaking off those who have not experienced him, Indra traverses many autumns.
He has become the counterpart to every form; that is his form for the sake of being perceived.
Indra moves in many forms through his magical powers (*māyā*); for ten hundred bay horses are yoked to him.
Yoking his two bay steeds to the chariot, Tvaṣṭṛ shines mightily here.
Who ever sits on the side of the hater, even while the patrons remain seated?
The gods came to a land where there was no pasture; though the earth was wide, it became narrow for them.
O Bṛhaspati, find a way out in this quest for cattle; O Indra, show the path to this singer here.
Day after day, he drove away the similar dark ones who were born in his dwelling, making one half [of the space] empty.
The bull struck down the two Dāsas, Varcin and Śambara, as they were plundering the enclosure.
Prastoka has now given you, O Indra, ten coffers and ten prize-winning horses as a gift.
From Divodāsa we have received the bounty of Atithigva; we have taken possession of the wealth belonging to Śambara.
Ten horses, ten chests, ten garments and provisions,
and ten lumps of gold— these I have received from Divodāsa. Ten chariots with side-horses and a hundred cows [I have given] to the Atharvans.
Aśvatha gave to Pāyu a great gift, beneficial for all people; Sārñjaya made offerings to the Bharadvājas who brought such wealth.
O Lord of the Forest, may you be firm of limb, our friend, a deliverer, and a source of noble heroes.
Bound with cow-hides, be firm; let your rider conquer all that is to be won.
From heaven and from earth its vigor has been brought forth; from the trees its conquering power has been gathered.
Worship with an oblation the chariot of Indra—the thunderbolt of waters, encompassed by cow-hides and endowed with might.
The thunderbolt of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, the navel of Varuṇa—O divine chariot, enjoying this our offering of oblations, accept these gifts.
Make the earth and the sky resound; let the world, established in many places, take heed of you.
O drum, in harmony with Indra and the gods, drive our enemies far, even further away.
Thunder forth strength and vigor for us; roar aloud, driving away all misfortunes.
Snort them away from here, O drum; you are the fist of Indra—be firm!
O driver, bring them back; the drum speaks aloud as our banner. Our men, winged with horses, move together; O Indra, let our chariot-warriors be victorious!
Sacrifice after sacrifice, and song after song, I offer to Agni for his skill.
Again and again we shall praise the immortal Jātavedas, like a beloved friend. Let us serve the Son of Strength with offerings, for he is well-disposed toward us;
may he be our protector in battles, our increaser, and the savior of our bodies.
For you, O Agni, are a bull, ageless and great; you shine with your flame.
Blazing with your unfailing luster, O pure one, shine brightly with your beautiful beams.
You worship the great gods; you shall sacrifice to them in succession through your wisdom and your wondrous power.
Turn hither, O Agni, for our protection; grant us strength and win it for us!
Him whom the waters, the stones, and the forests nourish as the embryo of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), he who is born by men through forceful friction upon the high ridge of the earth.
He who has filled both worlds with his radiance hastens through the sky with smoke;
he has been seen through the darkness in the nights—he, the dark and ruddy bull, the dark and ruddy bull.
O divine Agni, with your lofty flames and your bright luster!
O most youthful one, being kindled among the Bharadvājas, shine upon us with wealth, O bright one; shine with splendor, O purifier!
You, O Agni, are the lord of the house for all the human tribes.
O most youthful one, protect your kindler from distress with a hundred fortresses for a hundred winters, as well as those who give to your praisers.
O Vasu, O Citra, impel our gifts with your aid.
O Agni, you are the charioteer of this wealth; find a firm footing for us and our offspring. Carry across our children and descendants with your unfailing, tireless protectors.
O Agni, ward off from us the divine wrath and the godless deceptions.
O friends, with a new hymn, milk the cow that yields nectar; release her who does not shrink away.
She who has milked immortal fame for the self-luminous host of Maruts;
she who is in the favor of the swift Maruts, she who moves with auspicious ways—
she has twice milked [her bounty] for Bharadvāja.

I praise him for my purpose, like Indra of excellent wisdom, like Varuṇa possessed of creative power, like Aryaman the delightful one who provides abundant nourishment, and like Viṣṇu— the one who milks all cows and bestows food that sustains all.

Like the brilliant host of Maruts, loud-sounding, may he bring together the invincible Pūṣan so that he may gather hundreds and thousands from the people; may he make the hidden treasures manifest, and may he make wealth easy for us to find.
O Pūṣan, hasten toward me! I would whisper into your ear, O glowing one.
The hostile enmities of the enemy—
do not uproot the *kākambīra* tree, for you shall utterly destroy the revilers; nor indeed, O Hero, do they seize the necks of the bird even for a single day.
May your friendship be like that of a skin free from predators—
unpierced, flowing with milk, and full to overflowing.
For you are beyond mortals, equal even to the gods in splendor.
O Pūṣan, look upon us in battles; do you now protect us as you did of old.
O shakers, may the lovely guidance of the lovely one be ours—may the truth of the god be ours, O Maruts, for the mortal who strives to sacrifice, O you who are worthy of worship.
Even instantly, the praise of whom the god Sūrya goes around the sky;
the Maruts have assumed brilliant power, a name worthy of sacrifice, Vṛtra-slaying power—the most excellent Vṛtra-slaying power.
Once indeed the heaven was born; once the earth was born.
The milk of Pṛśni was milked but once; no other is born after it.
I praise the people of holy vows with newest songs—Mitra and Varuṇa, who grant favor.
May they come hither; may they hear us here: the noble rulers Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni.

Worthy of praise by every people at the sacrifices, the one of undaunted will, the delighter of the two young maidens—Agni, the child of heaven, the son of strength, the banner of the sacrifice, the ruddy one, I shall worship.
The two daughters of the ruddy one are of different forms; one is adorned with stars, the other with rays.
Moving swiftly together, purifying, they reach the heard prayer as it is recited in verse.

Toward Vāyu, the great inspired thought goes forth—toward him who possesses vast wealth, who grants all boons, and who fills the chariot. With your shining path, O master of the teams, you, the sage, seek the sage, O most worshipful one.

May that radiant chariot of the Aśvins, which covers my body and is yoked by thought, bring you hither— O Nāsatyas, O Heroes— so that you may hasten on your path for the sake of our offspring and ourselves.
O Parjanya and Vāta, bulls of the earth, quicken the watery springs.
O sages who hear the truth, you who are the sustainers of the world, through your songs you have made the world what it is.
May Sarasvatī, the daughter of the lightning, of wondrous life, the wife of the hero, bestow inspired thought upon us.
In harmony with the divine dames, may she grant the singer a flawless refuge, an invincible protection.
With eloquence, he has approached the protector of every path, impelled by desire, with a song of praise.
May that Pūṣan grant us riches preceded by splendor; may he bring each and every prayer to fulfillment.
[The seers have praised] the god who receives the first portion, the glorious one, the bestower of vitality, the one with beautiful hands and lovely arms, the skillful master.
Let the Hotar priest worship Tvaṣṭar, the sacrificer of the dwellings, the radiant one who is easy to invoke.
With these songs, let us magnify Rudra, the father of the world, by day and by night. Impelled by the sage, let us separately call upon the great, lofty, undecaying, and most gracious one.
O youthful, wise, and worshipful Maruts, come to the longing of the singer.
For even the dull you enliven as you grow strong; thus do you, O heroes, approach like the Aṅgirases.
Lead forth the hero, the powerful and swift one, as a herdsman drives his cattle home.
He touches the body of the famous one with the rays of his speech, as a sage touches the firmament with his words. Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms for man when he was oppressed—
under your protection, which is being granted, may we rejoice in wealth, in our bodies, and in our offspring.
May Ahibudhnya with his waters, Parvata with his hymns, and Savitṛ grant us this favor. May Bhaga, who bestows gifts along with the plants, and Purandhi, quicken us toward wealth.
Now, [grant] us wealth borne on chariots, filling the people, rich in many heroes, the great guardian of Truth.
May we grant a dwelling that is undecaying, by which we may overcome the godless, rivaling people, and may we reach the god-fearing clans.
With prostrations, I invoke for you the goddess Aditi, and for mercy, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni;
and the bounteous Aryaman who is most gracious, the protecting gods, Savitar, and Bhaga.

O Sūrya, you of excellent light, father of Dakṣa, seek out the gods for sinlessness, O most mighty one— those twice-born ones who are followers of *ṛta*, truthful, radiant, worthy of sacrifice, and whose tongue is Agni. And may Heaven and Earth, the two worlds of great bliss, grant us wide dominion and a vast refuge.
O two Dhiṣaṇās, grant us great space and freedom so that there may be safety for our dwelling.
May the sons of Rudra, the invincible Vasus, being invoked today, be gracious to us. When we are beset by danger, whether small or great, we call upon the divine Maruts for aid.
To whom the two goddesses, Heaven and Earth, have clung, and whom Pūṣan follows as one who bestows ample sacrifice;
when you hear our call, O Maruts, and set out, all beings tremble on your distinguished path.
O singer, honor with a new prayer that hero Indra, the lover of songs.
May he hear our call when praised, and may he, being lauded, grant us great spoils of war.
O Waters, you who belong to men, bestow upon our children and descendants uninjured protection and well-being;
for you are the most motherly physicians, the progenitors of all that is stationary and all that moves.
May the divine Savitṛ, the protector, the golden-handed, the holy one, come to us;
he who, bounteous as the face of the dawn, discloses desirable treasures for the donor.
And you, O Son of Strength, may you turn the gods toward us today at this sacrifice.
May I ever abide in your bounty; O Agni, through your protection may I be rich in heroic sons.

And may those two Nāsatyas come to my invocation, for you, O sages, are indeed inspired by our prayers. Like Atri, you two heroes delivered him from great darkness; protect us from misfortune in the encounter.

May they be givers to us of splendid wealth, full of vigor, abounding in heroes and much food. May the divine ones, those of the earth, those born of the cow, and those of the waters, being gracious, grant us their favor, O gods.
May Rudra, Sarasvatī, Viṣṇu, and Vāyu, acting in harmony and being bounteous, be gracious to us.
May Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and the divine Vidhātṛ, as well as Parjanya and Vāta, cause our nourishment to swell.
And may that god Savitṛ, Bhaga, and Apāṃ Napāt, who bestows gifts, protect us;
may Tvaṣṭṛ, in harmony with the gods and their wives, and Dyaus with the gods, and Pṛthivī with the oceans, grant us aid.
May Ahi Budhnya hear us, and Aja Ekapād, Earth, and Ocean;
may all the gods, the increasers of *ṛta*, being invoked, and the hymns recited by sages, protect us when praised. Thus do the Bharadvājas, my grandsons, honor him with prayers and songs of praise.
The Gnas have been invoked, the unassailable Vasus; all you worshipful ones have been praised and have become present.
Up rises that great eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, the beloved and undeceivable.
The pure and beautiful face of *Ṛta* has shone forth like a golden disk at the rising of heaven.
The sage who knows the three assemblies of these gods and their births from of old—
Beholding both the upright and the crooked among mortals, the Sun surveys the deeds of the noble.
I praise you, the guardians of the great Truth— the boundless Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, the well-born.
I call toward Aryaman, Bhaga, and those of infallible thought, the purifiers who share in the feast.

I seek the Adityas with devotion— the destroyers of enemies, the lords of the virtuous, the undeceived, the great kings, the givers of fair dwellings, the youthful rulers of heaven with noble dominion, and Aditi herself.
O Father Heaven, O guileless Mother Earth, O Brother Agni, and O Vasus, have mercy on us!
O all you Ādityas and Aditi, being of one accord, extend to us manifold protection.
O worshipful ones, do not deliver us over to the wolf, nor to the she-wolf, nor to any who seeks to harm us.
For you indeed are the charioteers of our bodies; you have become the masters of skillful speech.
Let us not suffer for the sin committed by another, nor perform that deed which you, O Vasus, punish.
For you rule over all, O All-Gods; may the enemy himself bring harm upon his own person.
Homage indeed to the fierce one; I seek to win him with homage. Homage has supported both the earth and the sky.

Homage to the gods; homage is the lord of these. Even a committed sin I seek to expiate with homage. I [praise] you, the charioteers of *ṛta*, whose will is pure, who dwell in the abode of *ṛta*, the undeceived ones.
To those far-seeing heroes, all of you, I bow with prostrations, O great ones worthy of sacrifice.
For they possess the most excellent luster; they lead us across all difficulties.
Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni are good rulers, whose thoughts are fixed on *ṛta*, kings of speech, and true.

May Indra, Earth, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Aditi increase our strength, along with the five peoples; may they be providers of good shelter, good protection, and good guidance for us, being excellent deliverers and excellent guardians.
Now, O gods, come to the celestial dwelling; Bhāradvāja, the *hotṛ*, approaches you for your favor.
Seeking wealth, the sacrificer has praised with sacrificial foods the generations of the gods who sit near.
O Agni, Lord of the Good, drive away that crooked enemy, the thief of evil intent; make his path far distant and provide us a way of easy passage.
O pressing-stones, O Soma, you have indeed yearned for us for the sake of friendship.
Slay the greedy Pani, for he is a wolf.
For you, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your chief, are directed toward heaven.
May he make our path easy to travel on the journey and be our protector at home.
We have entered upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger,
by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.
I do not approve of that in heaven, nor on earth, nor by means of sacrifice, nor by these ritual labors.
May the well-formed mountains crush him; may the performer of excessive sacrifice fall low.
O Maruts, whoever holds us in contempt, or whoever seeks to find fault with the sacred formulation (*brahman*) as it is being performed—[may he be destroyed].
Let burning pains be his lot for his wicked deeds; may the sky scorch that hater of sacred prayer.
Why indeed, O Soma, do they call you the guardian of the sacred word? Why indeed do they call you our protector against curses?
Why indeed do you look with indifference upon us as we are being reviled? Cast your burning bolt at the hater of the sacred word!
May the dawns as they are born protect me; may the swelling rivers protect me.
May the firm mountains protect me; may the ancestors protect me at the invocation of the gods. May we always be of good mind; may we behold the sun as he rises.
So may the Lord of Wealths grant us wealth; may he, who never neglects the gods, come most readily with his protection.
May Indra come most quickly with his aid; may Sarasvatī, swelling with the rivers, come;
may Parjanya, bringing refreshment through the plants, come; and may Agni, well-praised and easy to invoke, come like a father.
O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation.
Sit down upon this sacrificial grass.
O Gods, he who honors you with an offering dripping with clarified butter—
Approach him, O all of you!
May the sons of Immortality hear our songs;
may they be gracious to us.
May all the gods, who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*) and hear our invocation according to the seasons,
enjoy the appropriate milk-offering. May Indra, accompanied by the host of Maruts, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, and Aryaman, accept our hymn of praise.
May they accept these our oblations.
O Agni, Hotṛ-priest, perform this sacrifice of ours according to the sacred ordinances, you who are wise among the divine host.
O All-Gods, hear this my invocation—ye who are in the mid-air and ye who dwell in heaven;
O you whose tongue is Agni, or ye who are worthy of sacrifice, sit upon this sacred grass and rejoice.
May all the Gods worthy of worship hear my prayer, as well as both Heaven and Earth and the Son of the Waters.
Let me not utter words that should be disregarded by you; may we, as your closest kin, rejoice in your favor.

Whosoever among the great ones, possessing the power of serpents, were born upon the earth, from heaven, or in the gathering place of the waters— may those gods grant us all life for our nourishment, bestowing wide space upon us through nights and mornings.
O Agni and Parjanya, you who are easily invoked, protect my prayer at this invocation; accept our well-spoken hymn of praise.
May one of you engender the sacrificial food (*iḷā*), and may the other produce the germ of life; bestow upon us nourishment accompanied by progeny.
Upon the strewn sacrificial grass, while the fire is kindled, I honor you both with a well-spoken hymn and great reverence.
O worshipful All-Gods, rejoice today in this our sacrifice at this oblation.
O Pūṣan, Lord of the Path, we have yoked you for our prayer, as one yokes a chariot for the winning of booty.
Lead us toward manly wealth, toward a hero who bestows sacrificial fees, and toward a desirable householder. O glowing Pūṣan, urge even the one who is unwilling to give toward giving.
Even from the gambler, soften the mind; clear the paths for the winning of booty; drive away the adversaries. May our prayers be successful, O Mighty One!
O Sage, pierce through the hearts of the Paṇis with your weapon;
then deliver them over to us. O Pūṣan, strike out with your weapon at the heart of the Paṇi, seeking what is dear to him.

O Pūṣan, O glowing one, with that goad which you carry, the stimulator of sacred prayer, scratch out his heart and tear it to pieces.
O glowing one, with that goad of yours which has a cow for its ornament and which subdues cattle.
We pray for thy favor;
and make our prayer one that wins cattle, wins horses, and wins booty, so that it may be like a hero for our enjoyment.
O Pūṣan, bring us together with one who knows, who may directly instruct us and say, "This is indeed it.
May we go together with Pūṣan, who shall point out our home.
Saying,
"These indeed [are they]," Pūṣan’s wheel is not harmed; the felly does not fall away, nor does its rim waver.
Pūṣan does not forget him who honors him with an oblation;
he is the first to find wealth.
May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses.
May Pūṣan win booty for us.
O Pūṣan, follow after the cows of the sacrificer who presses the soma,
and also those of us who offer praise.
Let none of us perish, let none be harmed, let none be shattered in a pit;
therefore, come hither with those who are unharmed. We call upon Pūṣan, who hears us, whose wealth is never lost.
We seek the Lord of wealth.
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never come to harm;
we here are your praisers.
May Pūṣan place his right hand around us from afar;
may he bring back to us what we have lost. Come, O son of liberation, O glowing one; let us two be united.
Be the charioteer of our *ṛta*.
We implore the best of charioteers, the one with braided hair, the lord of great bounty, the friend of wealth.
O glowing one, you are a stream of wealth; O Vasu, you are a mass of riches for those whose steeds are goats.
You are the friend of every devotee.
Now let us praise Pūṣan, the possessor of goats as his steeds, the winner of prizes.
The brother-in-law is called the lover of his sister. I have spoken to the suitor of my mother; let the lover of my sister hear us. He is the brother of Indra and my friend.
May the goats, firmly seated upon the chariot, carry Pūṣan— the god who brings glory to men— bearing him along.
He who points him out, saying, "Pūṣan has eaten the groats."
Not by that [strength] is the god to be invoked;
rather, he who is the best of charioteers, the lord of the virtuous, joined as a friend— Indra, with him as his ally, smites the Vṛtras.
And there, upon the speckled ox, the best of charioteers brought down the golden wheel of the Sun.
Whatever we may say to you today, O much-praised, wondrous, and wise one—
Make that prayer of ours successful;
and lead this host of ours, seeking cattle, to the winning of booty.
O Pūṣan, you are renowned from afar.
We implore from you a blessing that drives away evil, bringing wealth near;
for well-being today and for well-being tomorrow. O Indra and Pūṣan, we [call upon you] for friendship and for our welfare.
Let us invoke him for the winning of booty.
One [Soma] has approached to drink the pressed juice from the two bowls;
the other desires the groats.
The goats are the carriers of one; the two bay steeds are prepared for the other.
With these two, he strikes down the Vṛtras.
When Indra, the most virile, led forth the great waters according to the sacred law.
Pūṣan was there with us. We grasp that benevolence of Pūṣan and of Indra, as one would grasp the branch of a tree.
We draw Pūṣan toward us, as a charioteer draws the reins;
we draw Indra for my great well-being.
One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; like the sky, you possess two days of different aspects.
For you protect all wondrous powers, O self-dependent one; O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious for us.

With goats for steeds, guardian of cattle, whose home is strength, who quickens the prayer, he is established throughout the entire world. Brandishing his supple goad, Pūṣan, the god, moves along as he surveys all living beings.
O Pūṣan, those golden ships of yours that travel within the ocean and through the mid-air— with those you go on an embassy for Sūrya, seeking glory and impelled by desire.
Pūṣan is the close kinsman of heaven and earth, the lord of nourishment, the munificent one of wondrous luster.
RV 6.58.4: Him whom the gods gave to Sūryā—him who was created by desire, powerful and swift-moving.
RV 6.59.1: Now, while the juices are pressed, let me proclaim those heroic deeds which you two have performed.
RV 6.59.2: Your fathers, the enemies of the gods, have been slain; O Indra and Agni, you two live.
Truly, O Indra and Agni, such is your greatness that it is most worthy of praise;
you have a common father, and you two are twin brothers here, with the same mother. Having settled together at the pressed juice, like two horses yoked to a feast.

Now we invoke Indra and Agni, the wielders of the thunderbolt, here for our protection, O gods. O Indra and Agna, you who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*), when one praises you while the juices are pressed—
O gods, you who enjoy the pure oblation, you do not consume even a word spoken with pleasure.
O Indra and Agni, what mortal man among you two gods understands this?
One of you, having yoked his horses that go in different directions, speeds along on the same chariot.
O Indra and Agni, this footless one has come before those who have feet.
Having cast off its head, it moves along, speaking loudly with its tongue; it has stepped down thirty paces.
O Indra and Agni, for the men stretch their bows in their arms against us.
Do not abandon us in this great contest for wealth, in the quests for cattle.
O Indra and Agni, the hostilities of the enemy oppress me.
Drive away our enemies and keep us far from the sun.
O Indra and Agni, yours indeed are the treasures of heaven and of earth.
Bestow upon us here wealth that nourishes all our lives,
O Indra and Agni, who are borne by hymns and hear our invocation through our praises;
come hither with all our songs for the drinking of this Soma.
He pierces Vṛtra and wins booty— the one who shall worship Indra and Agni,
the two victorious ones. May they, ruling over abundant wealth, most powerful through their might,
and striving for victory, — those two, O Indra and Agni, now fight for the cattle, for the waters, for the sun, and for the dawns that have been carried away.
O Indra, you take for yourself the quarters, the sun, the dawns, the bright waters, and the cows; O Agni, you come with your team of horses.
O Vṛtra-slayers, Indra and Agni, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying powers and our reverent salutations. O Indra and Agni, through your guileless and most excellent gifts, be present with us.
I invoke those two by whom all this that was done of old has been encompassed— Indra and Agni, who do not fail us. Fierce destroyers of adversaries, Indra and Agni we invoke.
May they be gracious to us in such a state.
O lords of the virtuous, slay the Aryan enemies; slay the Dāsa enemies;
slay all those who hate us.
O Indra and Agni, these hymns have resounded toward you both; drink the pressed juice, O you who bring auspiciousness!
O Heroes, those many-desired teams of yours which exist for the donor— 6.60.7–8.1.
O Indra and Agni, come hither with those [hymns].
With those, O heroes, come to this pressed libation;
O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
Praise him who, with his flame, embraces all the forests and makes them black with his tongue.
That mortal who, having kindled him, seeks to win the favor of Indra.
For glory, [drive] the waters across easily;
O you two, grant us food accompanied by strength and swift horses to carry Indra and Agni.
I invoke you both, O Indra and Agni; may you both rejoice together in the gift of wealth. You both are the givers of food and riches; I call upon you both for the winning of booty.
Come to us with herds of cattle, with horses, and with treasures.
We invoke those two gods, Indra and Agni, the friends who bring auspiciousness, for friendship.
O Indra and Agni, hear the call of the sacrificer who presses the soma;
enjoy the oblations, come hither, and drink the honeyed soma.
This [Sarasvatī] bestowed upon Vadhryaśva, who had offered oblations, the impetuous Divodāsa, the deliverer from debt.
She who has utterly devoured the Paṇi, the consumer of all—those are thy mighty gifts, O Sarasvatī.
She, like one digging for lotus-stalks, has shattered the ridges of the mountains with her surging billows and her powerful waves.
With well-fashioned hymns and inspired thoughts, let us invoke Sarasvatī for our protection, she who slays the Pārāvatas.
O Sarasvatī, strike down those who revile the gods; strike away the progeny of every deceitful Bṛsaya.
Moreover, O possessor of plenty, you have found fertile lands for the people, and you have brought forth flowing waters from the uneven places.
May the goddess Sarasvatī, rich in spoils, protect us with her bounties;
may she, the guardian of inspired thoughts, aid us. O Goddess Sarasvatī, whoever invokes you when the prize is at stake—
Like Indra in the conquest of Vṛtra.
O Goddess Sarasvatī, you who are swift in the prize-contests, protect us; like Pūṣan, grant us gain.
And may Sarasvatī, the terrible one whose path is golden, the slayer of Vṛtra, desire our fair praise—
she whose [power] is infinite, unyielding, brilliant, moving, and ocean-like.
Moving unassailable, she roars aloud; she,
the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*), has extended herself beyond all our enemies like sisters,
just as the sun [spreads its light].

And may Sarasvatī, who is dear among the dear, who has seven sisters, and who is well-beloved, be worthy of our praise. Having filled the earthly realms, the wide expanse, and the mid-air, she has pervaded all.
May Sarasvatī protect us from the revilers.
Abiding in three places, sevenfold, she who causes the five tribes to prosper—
may she be invoked in every contest for booty.
She who is distinguished among the mighty by her greatness, who excels all others in splendor and in her work—Sarasvatī, vast as a chariot, fashioned for wide power, is to be praised by the wise.
O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater wealth; do not cast us away, nor fail us with your milk.
Be pleased with our friendship and our kinship; let us not go from you to desolate lands.

I praise the two heroes who rule over this heaven; I, chanting with hymns, invoke the Aśvins, those who at the breaking of dawn instantly strive to reach the ends of the earth across the wide expanses.
Moving toward the sacrifice with their pure [rays], they have caused the splendor of the chariot to shine through the regions of the air.
Measuring out many immeasurable boons, you two pass over the waters, the deserts, and the plains.
O ye two mighty ones, you have indeed carried away that eternal, unobstructed path; thus, with your horses, you have ever borne away our prayers.
With mind-swift, vigorous steeds, he hastens around to rest at the dwelling of the mortal who offers oblations.

May those two, the ancient and the youthful—yoked with their horses, honoring the prayer of the one who praises them anew—come hither, bringing splendor, nourishment, food, and strength; let the ancient, guileless Hotar-priest worship them.
Those two lovely, wondrous ones, most effective in many ways, the ancient ones, I seek to win with a new hymn—
those who have become the greatest bringers of bliss to him who praises and lauds, bestowing brilliant gifts upon the singer.
As such, you carried Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, out from the waters and the ocean by means of your birds through the mists of air.
Traversing leagues with dustless, winged steeds from the lap of the ocean, you two chariot-borne victors shattered the mountain.
O bulls, having heard the call of Vadhrimatī, you granted boons to Śayu and caused his cattle to swell;
thus, O swift-moving ones, you brought forth the favor of Cyavāna.
Whatever wrath of the gods or among mortals has existed from of old, O Heaven and Earth—
O Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudriyas, bestow that burning evil upon him who is allied with the Rākṣasas.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, the two kings, take notice of him who knows the two realms of space and ordains them according to the seasons.
Cast your weapon at the deep-seated demon, at the treacherous speech of the deceitful Ānava.
With your inner wheels, come on your radiant, hero-bearing chariot to the dwelling of our son.
With your secret abandonment, strike off the heads of the mortal who seeks to harm us.
Come hither with your teams of horses—the highest, the midmost, and even the lowest—toward us!
O you of wondrous bounty, open the doors of the firm stall filled with cattle for the one who sings your praise.
Where has the reverent hymn of praise, like a messenger, not found those two beautiful ones today, they who are invoked by many?
RV 6.63.1: O Nāsatyas, he who has turned you hitherward—since you are most dear to this man’s prayer.
RV 6.63.2: Come readily to this my invocation, being praised, so that you may drink the soma-juice;
you shall go around that path of yours, lest any harm from beyond or within should overcome us.
The praise has been offered for the soma-juice; the sacrificial grass has been spread in the wide space, most easy of access.
With uplifted hands, seeking you both, we have paid homage as the pressing-stones reach you, anointing you.
Agni has stood upright at your sacrifices; the glowing ladle, dripping with ghee, goes forth toward you.
The Hotṛ-priest, joyfully minded and chosen, has harnessed himself for the invocation of the two Nāsatyas.
For the sake of glory, the daughter of Sūrya mounted the chariot, O you who possess many enjoyments, it being a hundredfold protection.
Through your wondrous powers, O masters of magic, you became manifest here at the birth of the two heroes, the ones worthy of sacrifice among men.
With these glorious and beautiful splendors, you two brought prosperity to Sūryā for her wedding.
Birds flew forth after you for the sake of your wondrous form; let our well-praised hymn reach you, O ye worthy of worship.
May your birds, your most excellent horses, carry you toward the offerings, O Nāsatyas.
Your chariot, swift as thought, has been let loose, following many nourishing streams of food.
For manifold indeed is your gift, O you who enjoy many things; swell for us the inexhaustible cow of nourishment.
And may both praise and beautiful hymn be yours, O lovers of sweetness, as well as the juices that have followed your bounty.
Moreover, Puraya gave me two swift, ruddy mares; Sumīḷha, a hundred; and Peruka, cooked offerings.
Śāṇḍa gave me golden ornaments and ten well-disposed, high-born cows that follow my will.
O Nāsatyas, Purupanthas has given you a hundred and a thousand horses for my song.
O hero, you have indeed granted [boons] to the song of Bharadvāja; may the demons be struck down by you, the one of many wondrous deeds.
May we abide in your favor within the wide expanse together with the patrons.
The Dawns have risen up, radiant with splendor, shining like the white waves of the waters.
She makes all paths easy to travel and pleasant to go upon; the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) has become wealthy, bountiful, and free from want.
Auspicious, you have appeared, shining far and wide; your flames and rays have flown up to the sky.
Adorning yourself, you make your breast visible, O Goddess Dawn, shining with your days.
The ruddy, radiant bulls draw her as she spreads far and wide, the fortunate one.
She drives away the darkness like a hero against his enemies; the swift maiden, newly wedded, repels the gloom.
Thy paths are easy to traverse and fair upon the mountains; O self-luminous one, thou dost cross over the waters unassailed.
O daughter of heaven, O noble one, bring hither to us wealth upon your broad path, so that we may enjoy it.
O Dawn, you bring [wealth] with your yoked horses; unassailed, you carry your chosen boon according to your pleasure.
O daughter of heaven, you who are a goddess, you have become beautiful through your greatness at the first invocation.
RV_06.064.06.1 Your vital strengths...
RV_06.065.01.1 This daughter of heaven, born from the sky, awakening the human settlements, has now awakened them.
RV_06.065.01.2 She who, with her radiant light, has become manifest throughout the nights, even piercing through the darkness of the gloom.

They have gone forth with their ruddy-yoked horses; the Dawns, with their radiant chariots, shine forth in splendor. Leading the forefront of the great sacrifice, they drive away the darkness of the night.
Bringing renown, booty, nourishment, and strength, the Dawns bestow these gifts upon the mortal who offers oblations.
O wealthy ones, ruling over heroic sons, bestow protection today and grant treasure to the one who serves you.
For now, O Dawns, there is treasure for the one who serves you; now, for the hero who offers oblations;
now, for the inspired singer who chants his hymns. You have indeed brought this even to one like me from of old.
For now, O Dawn who dwellest on the mountain ridges, the Aṅgirases sing to thee for the sake of the stalls of cattle;
with song and prayer they have split them open, and the invocation of men has become effective.
Rise up from heaven, O Daughter of Heaven, as of old, for us who worship thee like Bharadvāja, O Bounteous One!
Bestow upon the singer wealth with noble heroes; grant us far-reaching renown.
Let that form be a marvel even to the wise, though it bears the common name of "cow.
One [form] swells among mortals for milking; Prisni, having once milked her bright udder, has yielded her milk.
Those Maruts who, like fires placed upon their altars, have blazed forth, having grown strong twice and thrice;
they have become free from want, golden-hued, and endowed with manly vigor and heroic powers all at once.
They are the sons of the bounteous Rudra, whom the steadfast one has brought forth to support.
For the Great Mother, she who is vast, has seen the great one; that dappled cow has brought forth the embryo for the noble one.
They do not shrink from their birth, though they are within [the womb], purifying themselves from all reproaches.
When the bright ones have been milked out according to their pleasure, they sprinkle their bodies with splendor.
Swiftly they come, among whom no one is left behind even for the milking; assuming their bold names, the Maruts are present.
They who are not stingy, tireless in their greatness, and never failing in their bounty—O powerful ones, do not hide from us.
These very fierce ones, with their bold armies, have joined together both well-established worlds by their might.
Now indeed among these [Maruts], who possess their own radiance and impetuous power, Rodasī stands like a light.
O Maruts, this journey of yours is blameless; even he who has no horse and no chariot is driven along by it.
Without reins and without bridles, crossing the mid-air, it traverses the two worlds, making the paths straight.
There is no one to ward him off, nor any to overcome him, O Maruts, whom you protect in the contest for booty.
He who wins offspring, cattle, progeny, or water—he shall burst open the enclosure on the decisive day of battle.
Bring forth a brilliant hymn for the singing host of the Maruts, the swift and self-strong.
RV 6.66.9: Those who by their might overcome all powers—O Agni, the earth trembles before those champions.
RV 6.66.10: Radiant like the flash of a sacrifice, like the eager tongues of Agni, the Maruts are like roaring heroes; born in splendor, they are unassailable.
I invoke with my invocation that increasing host of Maruts, whose spears are flashing, the sons of Rudra.
For the host of heaven, the pure hymns of the mind have vied like fierce waters rushing from the mountains.
With songs of praise, I would magnify you two, Mitra and Varuṇa, the most eminent among all existing beings.
They who, like reins, have well controlled and guided two peoples with their own arms, being most excellent and peerless—
this prayer of mine is spread out for you both upon the dear sacrificial grass with reverence.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, bestowers of good gifts, grant us that invincible protection which is your secure refuge.

Come hither, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with fair praise, being invoked with beloved homage. You two unite the people like craftsmen with their work; you strive for even those who listen with your greatness.
Like two prize-winning horses, you whose kin are purified, when Aditi bore the germ according to the Eternal Law (Ṛta).
You two who were born great, being exceedingly great, have established yourselves as terrible ones for the mortal enemy.

When all the gods, rejoicing through your greatness and acting in harmony, bestowed sovereign power upon you both; when you encompassed even the two wide worlds, your spies are undeceived, unerring, and vigilant.
For you two maintain sovereign power day after day; you make firm the ridge of heaven as if from near at hand.
Firm is the constellation, belonging to all the gods; it has stretched out the earth and the sky with its milk for the two who are free from disease.
You two have fashioned a wide belly to be filled, which they fill together when they sit in the assembly.
The young maidens do not cease from their labor when they bring forth the all-enlivening milk that has been stirred.
With our tongue we shall partake here of this, O wise ones, since the true messenger has appeared according to the *ṛta*.
Let that be your greatness, O you whose food is ghee: may you two most effectively drive away the distress of the donor.
When they vie against you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, and violate your dear laws established by you;

when those who are neither gods through their power nor mortals through sacrifice, like sons of the waters, scatter their speech as singers; and when some, reciting the *nivid* formulas with devotion, offer their praise.

Then we shall proclaim true hymns to you both; for in your greatness, you do not rival the gods. O Mitra and Varuṇa, under the protection of your shelter, grant us your aid here, so that the cattle may follow the straight-flying, bold, and vigorous steed as they are harnessed for the joy of battle.
At this sacrifice, the sacrificial grass is strewn; may you two, being of one mind and listening with favor, worship like Manu.

O Indra and Varuṇa, may he who turns toward us today for great nourishment and great well-being, bring us great fortune. For you two are the most excellent in the assembly of gods, the most powerful among the heroes by your own vigor.
Most bountiful among the wealthy, possessing great strength, you two overcome Vṛtra by means of *ṛta* with all your armies.
Praise those two, Indra and Varuṇa, who are eager for favor with your reverent hymns of praise.
One of them, with his thunderbolt and might, slays Vṛtra; the other, the sage, attends to the assemblies.
When all the wives and men have grown strong, and all the gods, self-praised among men;
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two have become great through your majesty, as have Heaven and Earth, the wide ones.
He indeed is the bounteous and self-strong one who, according to the *ṛta*, offers worship to you both, O Indra and Varuṇa, with his own self.
Through food, may he, the giver, cross over his enemies; may he win wealth and the people who possess wealth.

O Gods, that wealth which you two bestow upon the performer of the sacrifice—wealth consisting of treasures and abundant cattle—may that be ours, O Indra and Varuṇa, which shatters the curses of our adversaries.

And may there be for us, O Indra and Varuṇa, wealth that is well-protecting and guarded by the gods for our patrons— wealth whose vigor, prevailing in battles, instantly overcomes enemies through its splendor as a conqueror.
Now, O gods Indra and Varuṇa, being praised, bestow upon us wealth for the sake of glorious renown.
Thus praising the host of the Mighty One, may we cross over difficulties as one crosses waters with a boat.
Now offer a dear hymn to the sovereign Varuṇa, the lofty god, an expansive prayer.
He who, by his greatness, rules over the two wide worlds, whose law is mighty, shines through his wisdom like the undecaying one with his flame.

O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed juice, drink this pressed Soma, the intoxicating draught, you whose vows are firm. Your chariot comes toward the sacrifice for the feast of the gods, as it were to its own stall, for the drinking.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bulls, drink of the most honey-sweet, virile Soma.
This soma-juice has been poured out for us; sit down upon this sacred grass and rejoice.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, through our ritual action and with nourishment, we impel you both toward the highest work.
Accept the sacrifice and bestow wealth upon us, carrying us across by paths that are free from harm.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the progenitors of all thoughts, the vessels that hold the Soma;
may our recited hymns favor you, and may our praises sung with chants protect you.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, lords of exhilaration, come to the Soma, bestowing wealth upon us.
May the prayers of our thoughts be united with you both through the nights; may the hymns being recited be joined with you through the songs of praise.

O Indra and Viṣṇu, may your horses, who overcome the assailants, carry you to the common feast. May you take pleasure in all the invocations of our thoughts; listen to my sacred formulations and my songs.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: in the exhilaration of Soma, you strode out widely. You made the mid-air more spacious and spread out the regions for our life.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, strengthened by the oblation, having accepted the first portion with reverence, you have been presented with the sacrificial gift.

O you who are fed with clarified butter, bestow wealth upon us; you are the ocean, the vessel that holds the Soma. O Indra and Viṣṇu, drink of this sweet Soma; O wonder-workers, fill your bellies. The intoxicating juices have come to you; listen to my prayers and my invocation.
You both have conquered; you are not defeated, nor has either of you been vanquished. O Indra and Viṣṇu, when you two strove together, you divided the thousandfold [booty] into three parts.
The two worlds are rich in ghee, the glory of all beings—vast, wide, yielding honey, and beautifully adorned.
Heaven and Earth, by the law of Varuṇa, are held apart, ageless and rich in seed.

Exhaustless, with many streams and full of milk, they yield clarified butter for the doer of good deeds, O ye of pure vows. Ruling over this world, O Heaven and Earth, pour upon us that seed which is beneficial to mankind.
O Heaven and Earth, O two Dhiṣaṇās, that mortal who offers worship to you both for the sake of upright conduct prospers;
he is born again through offspring according to the sacred law. From your union, diverse forms are poured forth, yet they share a common vow.
Heaven and Earth are enveloped in clarified butter; they are adorned with clarified butter, filled with clarified butter, and increased by clarified butter.
The two wide and broad ones, chosen as Hotṛ-priests and placed at the forefront—them indeed the inspired poets invoke for the sake of favor and for the sacrifice.
May Heaven and Earth sprinkle us with sweetness, they who drip sweetness, who yield sweetness, whose laws are sweet;
who bestow the sacrifice and wealth upon the gods, and grant us great renown, booty, and heroic strength.

May Heaven and Earth swell our strength for us—the Father and Mother, all-knowing and of wondrous deeds. May the two worlds, harmonious and bringing welfare to all, bestow upon us gain, booty, and wealth. Upward has that god Savitṛ, the skillful one, extended his golden arms for the sake of the sacrifice.
The liberal, youthful, and very skillful one sprinkles his hands with clarified butter while upholding the firmament.

May we abide under the most excellent impulse of the god Savitṛ, for the granting of wealth— Savitṛ who art the master of all bipeds and quadrupeds, both in their resting place and in their setting forth.
O Savitar, with your unfailing and auspicious protections, guard our household today. O golden-tongued one, for the sake of new prosperity, protect us; let no malevolent speaker have power over us.
Up has risen that god Savitar, the friend of the home, golden-handed, at the approach of evening.
The holy one with iron jaws and pleasant tongue brings forth abundant wealth for the donor. Savitar, of beautiful countenance, has stretched out his golden arms like an invoking priest;
he has ascended the heights of heaven and earth and has brought to rest every flying monster.
O Savitṛ, grant us what is desirable today, and what is desirable tomorrow; day by day, grant us what is desirable.
For, O God, through this prayer, may we be partakers of the desirable and of abundant dominion.
O Indra and Soma, great indeed is that majesty of yours; you two performed the first great deeds.
You two found the sun; you two found the light of heaven; you struck away all darknesses and insults.
O Indra and Soma, you cause the Dawn to shine; you lead forth the Sun together with its light.
You propped up the sky with a pillar and spread out the Earth, the Mother.
O Indra and Soma, you struck down Vṛtra who obstructed the waters; the heaven rejoiced after you. You set free the courses of the rivers and spread out the many oceans.
O Indra and Soma, you placed the cooked milk within the raw bellies of the cows.
You have seized within these bright and variegated moving worlds that which was unbound and radiant.
O Indra and Soma, you two indeed have bestowed a victorious, far-famed, and glorious gift that brings offspring.
You two, O fierce ones, have spread abroad among the people a manly strength that conquers armies.

Bṛhaspati, the mountain-shatterer, the first-born, the upholder of cosmic order (*ṛta*), the descendant of Aṅgiras, rich in oblations; he who dwells in the two worlds, the father, the bull with double stride, seated at the *gharma* vessel, roars aloud for us.
Bṛhaspati has indeed created a wide space for such a person as this when the gods are invoked.
Slaying the Vṛtras, he shatters the fortresses; conquering his enemies and foes, he prevails in battles.
Bṛhaspati has won all treasures; this god has seized the great stalls filled with cattle.
Desiring to win the waters and the light, unassailable, Bṛhaspati slays the adversary with his hymns of praise.
O Soma and Rudra, maintain your divine power; may our offerings reach you swiftly. Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, be auspicious to us—both to our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
O Soma and Rudra, drive away in all directions the disease that has entered our home.
Drive Nirṛti far away to a distance; may auspicious glories of renown attend us.
O Soma and Rudra, bestow all these healing remedies upon our bodies.
Untie and release from us whatever sin has been committed that is bound within our persons.
O Soma and Rudra, you who wield sharp weapons and sharp missiles, you who are most gracious—be merciful to us here!
Release us from the noose of Varuṇa and protect us with benevolent minds.
Like the appearance of a thundercloud is his countenance when the armored warrior advances into the lap of battle.
Conquer with an unpierced body; may the greatness of that armor protect you.
With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow the prize of battle; with the bow may we conquer fierce conflicts.
The bow frustrates the purpose of the enemy; with the bow may we conquer all the quarters.
As if about to speak, she goes toward the ear, embracing her dear friend;
like a woman, this bowstring twangs upon the stretched bow, carrying us across in the assembly.
Moving together like a woman to the assembly, may they bear [the arrow] in their lap like a mother her son.
May these two bow-ends, acting in concert and quivering, pierce the enemies and strike down the foes.
The father of many, he whose sons are many, makes a whizzing sound as he rushes into the fray. Fastened upon his back, the quiver, impelled by him, conquers all encounters and all hostile armies.
Standing on the chariot, the skilled charioteer leads the spirited horses forward, wherever he desires.
Marvel at the greatness of the reins: from behind, the traces follow the mind.
Making sharp sounds, the horses with strong hooves exert their strength together with the chariots.
Treading upon the enemies with their forefeet, they destroy the foes without ever faltering.
The chariot-stand is its oblation, and there its weapon and armor are laid down. May we always sit upon that auspicious chariot, being well-disposed in mind.
The Fathers, who sit at the sweet draught, bestowers of vitality, dwelling in hardship, powerful, and profound;
they who possess wondrous armies, whose strength lies in their arrows, who are never-failing, heroes in truth, vast, and conquerors of hosts.
O Brahmins, our Fathers, worthy of Soma—may Heaven and Earth, the auspicious and peerless, be gracious unto us.
May Pūṣan protect us from misfortune, O increasers of cosmic order; guard us, and let no one who speaks evil have power over us.
She clothes herself in beautiful feathers, her tooth is like a deer's; bound with cow-hides, she flies forth when discharged.
Where the heroes rush together and apart, there may the arrows grant us protection.
O *ṛjīti*, spare us; let our bodies be as stone.
May Soma speak for us, and may Aditi grant us protection.
They strike upon their haunches; they beat along the flanks.
O horse-whip, urge on the horses in battles for those who possess great wisdom.
Like a serpent with its coils, it encircles the arm, warding off the strike of the bowstring. The hand-guard, knowing all the ways, as a man, shall protect the man from every side.
Coated with lac, with a deer’s head, and having iron for its mouth—
this arrow, the offspring of Parjanya, to that divine shaft be great homage! Loosed forth, fly away, O arrow, sharpened by sacred prayer (*brahman*).
Go to the enemies; enter among them! Let not even one of the humans remain behind.
Where the arrows fly together like boys with unshorn hair—there may Brahmaṇaspati and Aditi grant us protection; may they grant us protection for all days.
I cover your vital organs with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality.
May Varuṇa make for you a space wider than the wide; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.
He who, whether our own kin, a stranger, or a foreigner, seeks to strike us down—
May all the gods protect him; may the sacred word (*brahman*) be my inner armor.
